summary:
Boxer, Calegari, Gee and Pilloni prove that every abelian surface and every genus two curve over a totally real field is potentially automorphic, and hence satisfies the Hasse–Weil conjecture: the completed zeta function has a meromorphic continuation to C and the expected functional equation. They also prove the potential modularity of genus one curves over quadratic extensions of totally real fields — new outside the totally real and the CM cases — and the existence of infinitely many modular abelian surfaces over Q up to twist with End_C(A) = Z, the first infinite family.

The obstruction the paper overcomes is that weight 2 Hilbert–Siegel modular forms occur only in the coherent cohomology of the Hilbert–Siegel modular variety, in degrees 0 to [F:Q], and not in the étale cohomology of any Shimura variety; abelian surfaces are irregular motives of weights (0,0,1,1), so the original Taylor–Wiles method does not apply, and the situation is closely analogous to the two-dimensional odd Artin conjecture. The main modularity lifting theorem, Theorem 8.4.1, says that for p ≥ 3 splitting completely in the totally real field F, a representation ρ : G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) with inverse cyclotomic similitude character, vast and tidy reduction, p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary at every place above p, pure at every finite place and ordinarily modular reduction, is modular.

Four bodies of work go into the proof. §3 constructs the Hilbert–Siegel Shimura varieties for G_1 = Res_{F/Q}GSp_4 and its subgroup G, with their integral models at the parahoric levels Kli(v), Si(v), Iw(v) and Par(v), their toroidal compactifications, and the Hecke action on the coherent cohomology of the automorphic vector bundles through cohomological correspondences and the Grothendieck–Cousin complex. §4 constructs higher Hida theory for GSp_4 over F, following Pilloni's construction for F = Q: working over the p-rank at least one stratum, which is not affine but has cohomological dimension one in the minimal compactification, the ordinary projector cuts out a perfect complex of amplitude [0,#I] rather than a projective module. §5 proves the doubling theorem, that the sum of the two degeneracy maps embeds two copies of the Klingen ordinary forms into the Iwahori ordinary forms; unlike every earlier incarnation of doubling this argument is geometric rather than a q-expansion argument, and rests on the behaviour of the operator Z_w = U_{Kli(w),1} − U_{Iw(w),1} along the w-non-ordinary locus, on the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism and on the identification of U_{w,2} with the square of the partial Frobenius. §6 develops higher Coleman theory on the adic generic fibre and proves the classicality theorem in an explicit slope range, together with the local constancy of the Euler characteristic which shows the complexes are balanced.

§7 then runs the Calegari–Geraghty modification of the Taylor–Wiles method twice, once with defect l_0 = 0 and once, after isolating a single place above p, with l_0 = 1; the trick that makes this possible is that p splits completely in F, so that only complexes with at most two terms occur and local–global compatibility need only be proved in degree 0, where doubling supplies it. The section also develops the GSp_4 analogue of Taylor's Ihara avoidance, through the nilpotent orbits of GSp_4 and their centralizers, and the big image conditions vast and tidy. §8 glues the resulting p-adic forms into a single classical form by analytic continuation, étale descent and the linear relations coming from doubling. §9 deduces potential modularity by a p–q trick and Moret-Bailly's theorem, and §10 shows that every mod 3 GSp_4-representation with inverse cyclotomic similitude character is the 3-torsion of infinitely many abelian surfaces, by proving that a twisted degree six rational cover of the Burkhardt quartic is unirational.

The atlas has essentially none of this. There is no GSp_4 anywhere, no Hilbert–Siegel Shimura variety, no higher Hida or higher Coleman theory, no modularity lifting for coherent cohomology or in irregular weight, and nothing on abelian surfaces, genus two curves or the paramodular conjecture. What it does have, and what this extraction imports rather than re-plans, is the abelian-scheme library, the PEL compactifications at good primes, the automorphic bundles, canonical subgroups and the Hodge–Tate map, Fredholm theory, the global and local deformation theory, the patching algebra including complexes with cohomology in several degrees, solvable base change and Moret-Bailly's theorem.

items.name: Conjecture 1.1.1: the Hasse–Weil conjecture
items.statement: Conjecture 1.1.1 (Hasse–Weil, after Serre). For a smooth projective variety X of dimension m over a number field F with good reduction outside S, the zeta function ζ_X(s) = ∏_x (1 − N(x)^{−s})^{−1}, taken over the closed points of a smooth proper integral model over O_F[1/S] and absolutely convergent for Re(s) > 1+m, extends to a meromorphic function on C; and there are A ∈ R^{>0}, nonzero rational functions P_v(T) for v | S and Gamma factors Γ_v(s) for v | ∞ such that ξ(s) = ζ_X(s)·A^{s/2}·∏_{v|∞}Γ_v(s)·∏_{v|S}P_v(N(v)^{−s}) satisfies ξ(s) = w·ξ(m+1−s) with w = ±1.

items.name: Theorem 1.1.2: the Hasse–Weil conjecture for genus two curves and abelian surfaces
items.statement: Theorem 1.1.2. Let X be either a genus two curve or an abelian surface over a totally real field F. Then Conjecture 1.1.1 holds for X.
items.locator: Theorem 1.1.2, deduced from Theorem 9.3.1 and Corollary 9.3.3, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501

items.name: Theorem 1.1.3: potential automorphy of genus two curves and abelian surfaces
items.statement: Theorem 1.1.3. Let X be either a genus two curve or an abelian surface over a totally real field F. Then X is potentially automorphic: there is a finite Galois extension L/F such that the compatible system 𝓡 attached to H^1(X_{Q̄},Q_p) is automorphic over L in the sense of Definition 9.1.1. In particular the L-function of H^1(X_{Q̄},Q_p) as a G_L-representation extends to a holomorphic function on C.
items.locator: Theorem 1.1.3, proved as Theorem 9.3.1 with Corollary 9.3.3, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501

items.name: Theorem 1.1.4: potential modularity of genus one curves over quadratic extensions
items.statement: Theorem 1.1.4. Let X be a genus one curve over a quadratic extension K/F of a totally real field F. Then X is potentially modular. The case K/F totally real was known from Taylor's potential modularity; the case K totally imaginary was proved in the ten-author paper; all other quadratic extensions, such as F = Q(√2) and K = Q(2^{1/4}), are new.

items.name: Theorem 1.1.5: infinitely many modular abelian surfaces with trivial endomorphisms
items.statement: Theorem 1.1.5. There exist infinitely many modular abelian surfaces A/Q up to twist with End_C(A) = Z. Consequently the L-function of H^1(A_{Q̄},Q_p) has a holomorphic continuation to C, which Theorem 1.1.3 alone does not give.

items.name: Theorem 1.1.7: the main modularity lifting theorem for abelian surfaces
items.statement: Theorem 1.1.7. Let F be a totally real field in which p > 2 splits completely, and let A/F be an abelian surface with good ordinary reduction at all v|p whose unit root crystalline eigenvalues are distinct modulo p at each v|p. Assume A admits a polarization of degree prime to p, and that the dual ρ̄_{A,p} : G_F → GSp_4(F_p) of the mod p representation on A[p] is vast and tidy. Assume ρ̄_{A,p} is ordinarily modular: there is an automorphic representation π of GSp_4/F of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2, ordinary at all v|p, with ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄_{A,p} and ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} pure at every finite v. Then A is modular, corresponding to a Hilbert–Siegel eigenform of parallel weight two.

items.name: The three cases in which the residual modularity hypothesis can be dropped
items.statement: Proposition 10.1.3 shows that the modularity hypothesis on ρ̄_{A,p} in Theorem 1.1.7 can be omitted when: (i) p = 3 and ρ̄_{A,3} is induced from a two-dimensional representation with inverse cyclotomic determinant over a totally real quadratic E/F in which 3 is unramified; (ii) p = 5 and ρ̄_{A,5} is induced from a GL_2(F_5)-valued representation with inverse cyclotomic determinant over such an E/F in which 5 is unramified; (iii) ρ̄_{A,p} is induced from a character of a quartic CM field H/F in which p splits completely.

items.name: The defect l_0 and the shape of the argument
items.statement: If the relevant coherent cohomology is nonzero in l_0+1 consecutive degrees one calls l_0 the defect; the original Taylor–Wiles method applies only when l_0 = 0, and the Calegari–Geraghty modification is needed when l_0 > 0. On the Galois side l_0 is the amount by which the sum of the dimensions of the local deformation rings falls short of the defect zero count. The strategy of the paper is to arrange that l_0 ≤ 1 by exploiting that p splits completely in F and by isolating one place v|p, so that only complexes with at most two terms occur, and so that local–global compatibility need only be proved in degree 0.

items.name: Klingen and Iwahori level at p and the Hecke operators U_{Kli(v),i}, U_{Iw(v),i}
items.statement: For an abelian surface A ordinary at v|p, the natural level at v for the associated Hilbert–Siegel eigenform is Klingen: a subgroup of order p inside A[v]. At Klingen level there are Hecke operators U_{Kli(v),1} with expected eigenvalue α_v + β_v and U_{Kli(v),2} with expected eigenvalue α_vβ_v; invertibility of the second is Klingen ordinarity and corresponds to ordinarity of ρ_{A,p}|_{G_{F_v}}. Iwahori level at v is a complete self-dual flag of subgroups of A[v]; there are two degeneracy maps from Iwahori to Klingen level and operators U_{Iw(v),1}, U_{Iw(v),2} = U_{Kli(v),2}, and the pullbacks of the expected form are Iwahori ordinary with U_{Iw(v),1}-eigenvalues α_v and β_v.

items.name: The local–global compatibility the higher Hida complexes carry
items.statement: Fixing a place v|p, the ordinary cohomology of the open subspace of the Hilbert–Siegel Shimura variety which is ordinary with Iwahori level at all w ≠ v and of p-rank at least one with Klingen level at v is a perfect complex of amplitude [0,1] whose Galois representation satisfies: for w|p with w ≠ v, ρ|_{I_{F_w}} is upper triangular with diagonal blocks 1, 1, ε^{−1}, ε^{−1} and a possibly nonzero entry between the first two; and at v the corresponding entry vanishes, so that ρ|_{I_{F_v}} has a two-dimensional unramified subquotient.
items.locator: §1.2, the two displayed matrices, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501

items.name: The group GSp_4, its similitude character, parabolics and level subgroups
items.statement: GSp_4 is the reductive group of symplectic similitudes of a rank four symplectic space, with similitude character ν; it is its own Langlands dual group. Its standard parabolic subgroups are the Siegel parabolic P (stabilizer of a Lagrangian) and the Klingen parabolic Q (stabilizer of a line), with Borel B and maximal torus T. For a place v the relevant compact open subgroups of GSp_4(F_v) are the hyperspecial GSp_4(O_{F_v}), the paramodular Par(v), the Siegel Si(v), the Klingen Kli(v), the Iwahori Iw(v) and its pro-v-unipotent radical Iw_1(v). The Weyl group W has order 8.
items.locator: §2.1 (Notation and conventions) and §3.3, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501

items.name: Induction of two-dimensional representations to GSp_4
items.statement: For a quadratic extension K/F and a representation r : G_K → GL_2 with determinant extending to G_F, the induction Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} r takes values in GSp_4 with a prescribed similitude character; explicitly the subgroup Δ ⊂ GL_2 × GL_2 of pairs with equal determinant embeds in GSp_4, and the wreath product GL_2 ≀ Z/2 acts. This is the source of the residually modular representations used in §10.
items.locator: §2.2 (Induction of two-dimensional representations), Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501

items.name: Lemma 2.1.3: semisimple GSp_4-representations are determined by GL_4 × GL_1
items.statement: Lemma 2.1.3. Let Γ be a group and L an algebraically closed field. A semisimple representation Γ → GSp_4(L) is determined up to conjugacy by the composite Γ → GSp_4(L) → GL_4(L) × GL_1(L), where the second factor records the similitude character.
items.locator: Lemma 2.1.3, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Gan–Takeda, Lemma 6.1)

items.name: The local Langlands correspondence for GSp_4 and L-packets
items.statement: Gan and Takeda's local Langlands correspondence rec_{GT} attaches to each irreducible smooth representation of GSp_4(K), K/Q_l finite, a Weil–Deligne parameter valued in GSp_4(C), grouping representations into L-packets; part (vii) of their main theorem characterises the generic member by holomorphy of the adjoint L-factor at s = 1. Definition 2.3.1: for a continuous ρ : G_K → GSp_4(Q̄_p) with p ≠ l, L(ρ) is the set of irreducible smooth Q̄_p-representations π of GSp_4(K) with rec_{GT,p}(π ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}) ≅ WD(ρ)^{F-ss}.
items.locator: §2.3 with Definition 2.3.1 and Remarks 2.3.2, 2.3.3, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Gan–Takeda, The local Langlands conjecture for GSp(4), Ann. of Math. 173 (2011), 1841–1882)

items.name: The Iwahori–Hecke algebra of GSp_4 and the Bernstein presentation
items.statement: For an Iwahori subgroup Iw(v) ⊂ GSp_4(F_v) the Hecke algebra 𝓗 has the Bernstein presentation with the θ_λ for λ ∈ X_*(T) and the T_w for w ∈ W; its centre is O[X_*(T)]^W, isomorphic to the spherical Hecke algebra by x ↦ e_{Sph(v)}x. Proposition 2.4.2: for x, y ∈ T(F_v)^+ one has [Iw_1(v)xIw_1(v)]·[Iw_1(v)yIw_1(v)] = [Iw_1(v)xyIw_1(v)], and these elements are units in 𝓗_1[1/p], indeed in 𝓗_1 if v ∤ p; so there is a homomorphism T(F_v) → (𝓗_1[1/p])^×.

items.name: Propositions 2.4.3 and 2.4.4: Iwahori invariants and Jacquet modules
items.statement: Proposition 2.4.3. For a smooth admissible Ē[G(F_v)]-module π the map π → π_U to the normalized Jacquet module induces an isomorphism of Ē[T(F_v)]-modules π^{Iw_1(v)} → (π_U)^{T(O_{F_v})_1}. Proposition 2.4.4. For χ : T(F_v) → Ē^× there is an isomorphism (π(χ)_U)^{ss} ≅ ⊕_{w∈W} Ē(w·χ). A principal series π(χ) is tame if χ is trivial on T(O_{F_v})_1 and unramified if χ is trivial on T(O_{F_v}).
items.locator: Propositions 2.4.3 and 2.4.4 with the definitions after them, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. items.name: Proposition 2.4.6: irreducibility and rec of principal series of GSp_4
items.statement: Proposition 2.4.6. (i) χ_1 × χ_2 ⋊ σ is irreducible if and only if none of χ_1, χ_2, χ_1χ_2^{±1} equals |·|_v^{±1}. (ii) For an irreducible constituent π, rec_{GT,p}(π)^{ss} = σ∘Art^{−1} ⊗ ((χ_1χ_2)∘Art^{−1} ⊕ χ_1∘Art^{−1} ⊕ χ_2∘Art^{−1} ⊕ 1). (iii) If χ_1 × χ_2 ⋊ σ is irreducible then the monodromy of rec_{GT,p} vanishes.
items.locator: Proposition 2.4.6, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Sally–Tadić; Roberts–Schmidt)

items.name: Definitions 2.4.9 and 2.4.11: Hecke parameters and general unramified principal series
items.statement: Definition 2.4.9. The Hecke parameters of an unramified π are the roots of the degree four polynomial Q_v(X), ordered so that the pairs (1,4) and (2,3) both multiply to the value γ_v of the similitude character at Frob_v; they are written [α_v, β_v, γ_vβ_v^{−1}, γ_vα_v^{−1}], labelling the vertices of a square. Definition 2.4.11. An unramified principal series π(χ) is general if the Hecke parameters are pairwise distinct and no ratio of them is q_v; then π(χ) is irreducible and |W·χ| = 8.
items.locator: Definitions 2.4.9 and 2.4.11, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501

items.name: Propositions 2.4.12, 2.4.13, 2.4.17 and 2.4.20: U_p-eigenvectors at Iwahori and Klingen level
items.statement: Proposition 2.4.12. For a general unramified principal series with Hecke parameters [α_v, β_v, q_vβ_v^{−1}, q_vα_v^{−1}], π^{Iw(v)} is a direct sum of eight one-dimensional simultaneous eigenspaces for the U^{naive}_{Iw(v),i}, with eigenvalues u_{v,0} = q_v^{−2}, u_{v,1} = α_v, u_{v,2} = q_v^{−1}α_vβ_v for each ordered choice of (α_v,β_v). Proposition 2.4.17 is the Klingen analogue: π^{Kli(v)} is a sum of four eigenspaces with u_{v,1} = α_v + β_v. Propositions 2.4.13 and 2.4.20 are the converses: an irreducible admissible π with such an eigenvector, no ratio of the parameters being q_v, is the unramified principal series with those Hecke parameters.

items.name: Lemma 2.4.15: the centre of the Iwahori–Hecke algebra of GL_2
items.statement: Lemma 2.4.15. The centre Z(𝓗_{Iw(v)'}[1/p]) of the Iwahori–Hecke algebra of GL_2 is generated by U^{GL_2}_{v,0} and q_vU^{GL_2}_{v,0}(U^{GL_2}_{v,1})^{−1} + U^{GL_2}_{v,1}; the Satake map e^{GL_2}_{Sph} is an isomorphism onto the spherical Hecke algebra and sends these to T^{GL_2}_{v,0} and T_{v,1}.
items.locator: Lemma 2.4.15, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501

items.name: Proposition 2.4.22: unipotent generic parameters and generic L-packets
items.statement: Proposition 2.4.22. Let r be unipotent. Then the L-packet corresponding to r contains a generic representation if and only if r is generic, that is if and only if ad(r^{F-ss})(1) has no invariants.
items.locator: Proposition 2.4.22, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Gan–Takeda, main theorem part (vii))

items.name: Ordinary and p-distinguished representations of GSp_4 and Proposition 2.4.24
items.statement: Definition 2.4.25. A cuspidal automorphic representation π of GSp_4(A_F) with central character |·|^2 and weight (k_v,l_v)_{v|∞}, k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 2 with k_v ≡ l_v mod 2, is ordinary if for each v|p the local component π_v is ordinary of weights k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 2. Proposition 2.4.24 classifies the ordinary p-distinguished π of weights k ≥ l ≥ 2 with ordinary Hecke parameters (α_v,β_v): if k > l > 3, or l = 2 and k > 2, then π is an irreducible principal series; if k = l = 2 then π is of Schmidt type Va when {α_v,β_v} = {1,−1}, IIIa when α_vβ_v = 1 but {α_v,β_v} ≠ {1,−1}, and a principal series otherwise.
items.locator: Proposition 2.4.24 and Definition 2.4.25, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Schmidt's tables)

items.name: Proposition 2.4.26: recognising ordinarity through invariant vectors
items.statement: Proposition 2.4.26. Let π be cuspidal of weight (k_v,l_v)_{v|∞} with k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 2 and central character |·|^2, and fix p-adic units (α_v,β_v)_{v|p}. Assume that for each v ∈ S_p either k_v > l_v > 3, or l_v = 2 and α_v ≠ β_v. With I' = {v ∈ S_p : l_v = 2} and I ⊆ I', π is ordinary with ordinary Hecke parameters (α_v,β_v)_{v|p} if and only if the corresponding eigenvector exists in the K_p(I)-invariants, where K_p(I) is Klingen at v ∈ I and Iwahori at v ∈ I^c.
items.locator: Proposition 2.4.26, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501

items.name: Propositions 2.4.28 and 2.4.30: characteristic polynomials from Iwahori-level eigenvectors
items.statement: Proposition 2.4.28. If π is an irreducible smooth Ē[GSp_4(F_v)]-module with (π^{Iw_1(v)})^{χ_v} ≠ 0 then for all σ ∈ W_{F_v} the characteristic polynomial of rec_{GT,p}(π)(σ) is the product of (X − χ_{v,i}(Art^{−1}σ)^{±1}) for i = 1, 2; if the four characters χ_{v,1}^{±1}, χ_{v,2}^{±1} are pairwise distinct then rec_{GT,p}(π) is the corresponding sum of characters. Proposition 2.4.30 is the Taylor–Wiles version: with central character |·|^2 and a nonzero localization at m_{ᾱ_1,ᾱ_2} with ᾱ_1^{±1}, ᾱ_2^{±1} pairwise distinct, rec_{GT,p}(π) = γ_1 ⊕ γ_2 ⊕ ε^{−1}γ_2^{−1} ⊕ ε^{−1}γ_1^{−1} with γ̄_i = λ_{ᾱ_i}.

items.name: Lemmas 2.4.33, 2.4.34, 2.4.36, 2.4.37 and Corollary 2.4.35: the Iwahori–Hecke algebra modulo p when q_v ≡ 1
items.statement: Lemma 2.4.33. If q_v ≡ 1 mod p there is a natural isomorphism 𝓗 ⊗_O k ≅ k[X_*(T) ⋊ W]. Lemma 2.4.34. For a smooth O[GSp_4(F_v)]-module M the inclusion M^{GSp_4(O_{F_v})} ⊂ M^{Iw(v)} is canonically split by [GSp_4(O_{F_v}) : Iw(v)]^{−1}e_{Sph(v)}. Corollary 2.4.35. For a smooth k[G]-module M, M^{Iw(v)} is a k[W]-module and M^{GSp_4(O_{F_v})} = (M^{Iw(v)})^W. Lemmas 2.4.36 and 2.4.37 translate the support of a finite-dimensional 𝓗 ⊗_O k-module at spherical and at Iwahori level under the condition that α_1, α_2, 1/α_2, 1/α_1 are pairwise distinct.

items.name: Purity of Weil–Deligne representations and Lemma 2.5.1
items.statement: A Weil–Deligne representation (V,r,N) of W_K with residue field of order q is pure of weight w if the monodromy filtration exists with the property that Frobenius acts on gr_i with all eigenvalues of absolute value q^{i/2}, equivalently if all the N^j : gr_{w+j}W → gr_{w−j}W are isomorphisms. Lemma 2.5.1. For a semisimple representation (V,r) of W_K there is at most one N making (V,r,N) pure, and if it exists it is the unique choice maximising n(r,N).

items.name: Lemma 2.6.1: archimedean L-parameters and their inductions
items.statement: Lemma 2.6.1. (i) Ind_{W_C}^{W_R} φ_{w,n} : W_R → GL_4(C) is conjugate to φ_{w,n} ⊕ φ_{w,n}. (ii) The composite φ_{(w;n,0)} : W_R → GSp_4(C) → GL_4(C) is conjugate to φ_{w,n} ⊕ φ_{w,n}. (iii) If φ : W_C → GL_2(C) has Ind_{W_C}^{W_R}φ conjugate to φ_{w,n} ⊕ φ_{w,n} and n ≠ 0 then φ is one of a determined pair. This classifies the archimedean components of the automorphic representations of GSp_4 of weight (2,2), which are non-degenerate limits of discrete series.

items.name: Theorems 2.7.1 and 2.7.2: Galois representations attached to cuspidal automorphic representations of GSp_4
items.statement: Theorem 2.7.1. Let F be totally real and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GSp_4(A_F) of weight (k_v,l_v)_{v|∞} with k_v ≥ l_v > 2, k_v ≡ l_v mod 2, and central character |·|^2. For each prime p there is a continuous semisimple ρ_{π,p} : G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) with ν∘ρ_{π,p} = ε^{−1} and, at each finite place v, WD(ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}), together with the prescribed Hodge–Tate weights and de Rham/crystalline conditions at v|p. Theorem 2.7.2 adds, for π unramified and ordinary at all v|p with ordinary Hecke parameters (α_v,β_v), that ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} is ordinary with the displayed block upper-triangular shape and unramified diagonal characters λ_{α_v}, λ_{β_v}, λ_{β_v}^{−1}ε^{−1}, λ_{α_v}^{−1}ε^{−1}.

items.name: Theorem 2.7.3: Galois representations for GL_2 over a quadratic extension of a totally real field
items.statement: Theorem 2.7.3. Let F be totally real, K/F quadratic with Gal(K/F) = {1,τ}, and 𝛑 a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(K) of weight 0 with trivial central character. Then there is a continuous irreducible ρ_{𝛑,p} : G_K → GL_2(Q̄_p) with WD(ρ_{𝛑,p}|_{G_{K_w}})^{ss} ≅ rec_p(𝛑_w ⊗ |·|^{−1/2})^{ss} for each finite w ∤ p, and with the expected behaviour under 𝛑 ≅ 𝛑^τ.

items.name: Strictly compatible systems, and Proposition 2.8.1 for abelian varieties
items.statement: A weakly compatible system of l-adic representations of G_F is strictly compatible if the Weil–Deligne parameters at every finite place, including those dividing l, are independent of l; it is pure of weight i if those parameters are. Proposition 2.8.1: for an abelian variety A over a number field F and 0 ≤ i ≤ 2 dim A, the groups H^i(A_{F̄}, Q̄_l) form a strictly compatible system, pure of weight i and defined over Q. Definition 2.8.2 writes ρ_{A,l} for H^1(A_{F̄},Q̄_l) and 𝓡_A for the compatible system, regarded as GSp_4-valued with multiplier ε_l^{−1} when A is a surface.

items.name: Conjecture 2.8.6 and Corollary 2.8.7: the conjectural functional equation for an abelian variety
items.statement: Conjecture 2.8.6 (Serre C9). For each i the completed L-function Λ_i(A,s) has a meromorphic continuation to C and satisfies Λ_i(A,s) = wN^{(i+1)/2−s}Λ_i(A,i+1−s) with w = ±1 and N ∈ Z_{≥1}. Corollary 2.8.7: it follows that Λ(A,s) has a meromorphic continuation with Λ(A,s) = εN^{−s}Λ(A,1+dim A−s), by Poincaré duality.

items.name: Arthur's classification for GSp_4 and Theorem 2.9.3
items.statement: Theorem 2.9.3. Let F be totally real and Π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_4(A_F) of symplectic type with multiplier χ. Then there is at least one discrete automorphic representation π of GSp_4(A_F) with central character χ transferring to Π; more precisely, choosing for each place v an element π_v of the L-packet corresponding to (rec_p(Π_v), χ_v), the representation π = ⊗'_vπ_v is automorphic and occurs with the multiplicity given by Arthur's multiplicity formula. Lemma 2.9.1 shows that a discrete π with the archimedean infinitesimal characters of φ_{(2;k_v−1,l_v−2)} which is not of general type has a compatible system of reducible Galois representations; Remark 2.9.2 records that in the general type case they are expected always to be irreducible.

items.name: The conditional status of Arthur's multiplicity formula for GSp_4
items.statement: The paper uses Arthur's multiplicity formula for the discrete spectrum of GSp_4 as announced by Arthur and proved by Gee–Taïbi. That proof is only as unconditional as Arthur's work for symplectic and orthogonal groups and the stabilisation of the twisted trace formula; in particular it depends on cases of the twisted weighted fundamental lemma announced by Chaudouard–Laumon whose proofs had not appeared, and on four references in Arthur's book which had not appeared publicly at the time of writing.

items.name: Locally finite operators and ordinary projectors
items.statement: Definition 2.11.1. An endomorphism T of an object M of Mod^{comp}(R) is locally finite if for all n ≥ 0 the quotient M/m_R^n is an inductive limit of finite type R-modules stable under T. Lemma 2.11.2: a product of commuting locally finite operators is locally finite. Lemma 2.11.3: T is locally finite on M if and only if it is locally finite on M/m_R. Lemma 2.11.4: if T is locally finite then lim_n T^{n!} converges pointwise to a projector e(T), the ordinary projector, with a T-stable decomposition M = e(T)M ⊕ (1−e(T))M on which T is bijective and topologically nilpotent respectively. The notion is extended to objects of the derived category D(R).

items.name: The similitude groups G_1 = Res_{F/Q}GSp_4 and its subgroup G
items.statement: Let F be totally real, V = O_F^4 with the O_F-linear symplectic form ⟨,⟩_1 given by J, and ⟨,⟩ = Tr_{F/Q}∘⟨,⟩_1. Then G_1 = Res_{F/Q}GSp_4 is the group of F-linear symplectic automorphisms of (V_Q,⟨,⟩_1) up to a similitude factor ν in Res_{F/Q}G_m, and G ⊂ G_1 is the subgroup with similitude factor in G_m, that is G = G_1 ×_{ν,Res_{F/Q}G_m} G_m. G admits a PEL Shimura variety with a moduli interpretation, integral models and integral compactifications; G_1 gives a Shimura variety of abelian type, and the connected components of the G_1-Shimura varieties are quotients of those of the G-Shimura varieties by finite groups, following Deligne's strategy for abelian type.

items.name: Definition 3.2.1: neat compact open subgroups
items.statement: Definition 3.2.1. For g = (g_l)_l ∈ G_1(A^∞), write Γ_{g_l} for the subgroup of Q̄_l^× generated by the eigenvalues of g_l under any faithful linear representation of G_1. Then g is neat if ∩_l (Q̄^× ∩ Γ_{g_l})_{tors} = 1, and a compact open subgroup is neat if all of its elements are; the prime-to-p variant drops the factor at p.
items.locator: Definition 3.2.1, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. items.name: The Shimura varieties for G and G_1 over C, and Lemmas 3.2.2 and 3.2.3
items.statement: Over C the Shimura varieties for G and G_1 are described by double cosets G(Q)^+\𝓗^{Hom} × G(A^∞)/K, with the arithmetic groups Γ(c,K) = G(Q)^+ ∩ cKc^{−1} and Γ_1(c,K). Lemma 3.2.2: ν(Γ_1(c,K)) = O_F^{×,+} ∩ ν(K). Lemma 3.2.3: for K neat the map Γ(c,K)\𝓗^{Hom} → Γ_1(c,K)\𝓗^{Hom} is finite étale with group Δ(K), where Δ(K) is the relevant finite quotient of totally positive units.

items.name: The parahoric level subgroups at v|p described by chains of lattices
items.statement: For v|p and the chain V_0 → V_1 → V_2 → V_3 → V_4 of O_{F_v}-lattices in F_v^4 with V_0 = ⊕O_{F_v}e_i and V_j = ⟨p^{−1}e_1,…,p^{−1}e_j,e_{j+1},…,e_4⟩, the relevant compact opens are GSp_4(O_{F_v}) = Aut(V_0) ∩ GSp_4(F_v) (hyperspecial), Par(v) = Aut(V_1 → V_3) (paramodular), Si(v) = Aut(V_0 → V_2) (Siegel parahoric), Kli(v) = Aut(V_0 → V_1 → V_3 → V_0) (Klingen parahoric) and Iw(v) = Aut(V_0 → V_1 → V_2 → V_3 → V_0) (Iwahori), each intersected with GSp_4(F_v).
items.locator: §3.3.1, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501

items.name: Definition 3.3.3 and the moduli problem 𝕐_K: reasonable level structures
items.statement: Definition 3.3.3. A level structure K = K^pK_p is reasonable if K^p ⊂ G(A^{∞,p}) is neat and K_p = ∏_{v|p}K_v with K_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v), Si(v), Kli(v), Iw(v)}. For such a K, 𝕐_K is the groupoid over AFF/Z_{(p)} whose objects over Spec R are quintuples (A,ι,λ,η,η_p): A → Spec R an abelian scheme, ι : O_F → End(A) ⊗ Z_{(p)} an action with Lie(A) locally free of rank 2 over O_F ⊗ R, λ : A → A^t a prime-to-p O_F-linear quasi-polarization whose kernel on A[v^∞] is trivial unless K_v = Par(v), when it has order p^2, η a K^p-level structure and η_p a K_p-level structure. The K_p-level structure is: H_v ⊂ A[v] of order p when K_v = Kli(v); L_v ⊂ A[v] of order p^2 and totally isotropic when K_v = Si(v); and a flag H_v ⊂ L_v ⊂ A[v] of orders p and p^2 with L_v isotropic when K_v = Iw(v). The K^p-level structure is a K^p-orbit of pairs (η_1,η_2) of O_F ⊗ A^{∞,p}-linear isomorphisms V ⊗ A^{∞,p} ≅ H_1(A_{s̄},A^{∞,p}) and F ⊗ A^{∞,p} ≅ F ⊗ H_1(G_m,A^{∞,p}) compatible with the symplectic pairings, with k ∈ K^p acting by (η_1k, ν(k)η_2).

items.name: Proposition 3.3.9: representability of the integral model Y_K
items.statement: Proposition 3.3.9. The groupoid 𝕐_K is representable by a quasi-projective scheme Π_0 : Y_K → Z_{(p)}^{×,+}\(A^{∞,p} ⊗ F)^×/ν(K^p)(1), whose morphism Π_0 has geometrically connected fibres; the complex points of a fibre are the corresponding classical Shimura variety Γ(c,K)\𝓗^{Hom}.

items.name: Lemmas 3.3.12, 3.3.13 and Proposition 3.3.17: the integral model for G_1
items.statement: The group (O_F)_{(p)}^{×,+} acts on Y_K by twisting the polarization. Lemma 3.3.12: the restriction of this action to O_F^{×,+}(K^p) = O_F^{×,+} ∩ ν(K^p) is canonically trivial. Lemma 3.3.13: for any geometric point x of Y_K the stabilizer of x for the action of (O_F)_{(p)}^{×,+} is exactly O_F^{×,+}(K^p), so the induced action of Δ is free. Proposition 3.3.17: there is a canonical map 𝕐_K^{G_1} → Y_K^{G_1} exhibiting Y_K^{G_1} as the coarse moduli space, with Π_0 : Y_K^{G_1} → (O_F)_{(p)}^{×,+}\(A^{∞,p} ⊗ F)^×/ν(K^p)(1) quasi-projective with geometrically connected fibres, and the map Y_K → Y_K^{G_1} is étale and surjective.
items.locator: Lemmas 3.3.12 and 3.3.13 and Proposition 3.3.17, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501

items.name: Proposition 3.4.1 and Corollary 3.4.2: local models and the geometry of the integral models
items.statement: Proposition 3.4.1. The scheme 𝕐_K is flat over Spec Z_{(p)}, normal and a local complete intersection (hence Cohen–Macaulay) of pure relative dimension 3[F:Q]; it is smooth if K_v = GSp_4(O_{F_v}) for all v|p, and in general smooth away from codimension 2. Corollary 3.4.2: Y_K^{G_1} is normal, flat over Spec Z_{(p)} and a local complete intersection.

items.name: Theorem 3.5.1 and Proposition 3.5.4: toroidal compactifications of the integral models
items.statement: Theorem 3.5.1. For a projective K-admissible polyhedral cone decomposition Σ there is a toroidal compactification X_{K,Σ} of Y_K, stratified by (G(Q)^+ ∩ K_p)\Σ/K^p = G(Q)^+\Σ/K, whose boundary is a relative Cartier divisor D_{K,Σ}; it carries a semi-abelian scheme extending A, is proper flat over Z_{(p)}, is a local complete intersection, and is functorial in Σ, the cohomology of ω^κ and ω^κ(−D) being independent of Σ. Lemmas 3.5.2 and 3.5.3 extend the action of O_{F,(p)}^{×,+} to X_{K,Σ} and show it factors through Δ and is free. Proposition 3.5.4: X_{K,Σ}^{G_1} is stratified by G_1(Q)^+\Σ/K, the map X_{K,Σ} → X_{K,Σ}^{G_1} is étale surjective, and for reasonable K the target is a normal flat local complete intersection over Z_{(p)}.

items.name: §3.6: Klingen and Siegel type correspondences and the degeneracy maps p_1, p_2
items.statement: Changing the level at a place w|p gives the correspondences used throughout. In the Klingen setting (Lemmas 3.6.4, 3.6.5 and Remark 3.6.6) there are proper surjective generically finite étale maps p_1 : Y_{K'} → Y_K forgetting the level structure H_w, and p_2 : Y_{K'} → Y_{K''} sending A to A/H_w^⊥, depending on a chosen x_w ∈ F^{×,+} which is a uniformizer at w and a unit at the other places above p; both descend to the G_1-models. In the Siegel setting (Lemmas 3.6.9 and 3.6.10) there are analogous maps p_1 forgetting L_w and p_2 : A ↦ A/L_w. Remark 3.6.8 warns that the notation K, K' and p_2 differs between the two settings.

items.name: §3.7: automorphic vector bundles ω^κ, weights for G and G_1, and their descent
items.statement: Over Y_K the prime-to-p isogeny class of abelian schemes gives a canonical Barsotti–Tate group 𝓖 with conormal sheaf ω_𝓖, which decomposes as ∏_{v|p}ω_{𝓖,v} under O_F ⊗ Z_p = ∏_{v|p}Z_p. A dominant algebraic weight for G is a tuple κ = (k_v,l_v)_{v∈S_p} with k_v ≥ l_v, classical if moreover l_v ≥ 2; the associated locally free sheaf is ω^κ = ∏_v Sym^{k_v−l_v}ω_{𝓖,v} ⊗ det^{l_v}ω_{𝓖,v}. A weight for G_1 is ((k_v,l_v)_{v∈S_p},w) with k_v − l_v ≡ w mod 2 and w even, fixed to be w = 2; for each such w, multiplication by ∏_v v(x)^{(k_v+l_v−w)/2} defines an effective descent datum on ω^κ along the étale map Y_K → Y_K^{G_1}, giving the sheaf ω^κ on Y_K^{G_1}. Remark 3.7.3 gives the corresponding descent datum for ω^κ in characteristic p when k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 0 mod (p−1).

items.name: Lemma 3.8.2 and Proposition 3.8.3: independence of Σ and the splitting for G_1
items.statement: Lemma 3.8.2. The complexes RΓ(X_{K,Σ},ω^κ), RΓ(X^{G_1}_{K,Σ},ω^κ), RΓ(X_{K,Σ},ω^κ(−D)) and RΓ(X^{G_1}_{K,Σ},ω^κ(−D)) are independent of Σ. Proposition 3.8.3: the pullback maps RΓ(X^{G_1}_K,ω^κ) → RΓ(X_K,ω^κ) and likewise with (−D) split in the derived category of Z_p-modules, which is what transfers good properties from the moduli space X_K to X_K^{G_1}. Lemma 3.8.5 is the underlying fact that for a finite étale morphism with Galois group G one has f_*O_T = O_S ⊕ I_G ⊗_{Z[G]} f_*O_T.

items.name: §3.8: Grothendieck duality, fundamental classes and traces for lci correspondences
items.statement: For an embeddable morphism f : X → Y of embeddable S-schemes which are local complete intersections of pure relative dimension n, Lemma 3.8.9 gives f^!O_Y = K_{X/S} ⊗ f^*K_{Y/S}^{−1} invertible; Lemma 3.8.10 is the compatibility of f^! with restriction to the vanishing locus of a section h of a line bundle on Y when neither h nor f^*h is a zero divisor; Lemma 3.8.12 computes the fundamental class in the finite flat smooth case as det(df) = tr_f; Lemma 3.8.15 shows the fundamental class Θ : O_X → f^!O_Y restricts to O_X(−D_X) → f^!O_Y(−D_Y) under normal crossings hypotheses; and Proposition 3.8.17 gives the commutative diagram comparing the trace on K_X(−(n−1)D') with the twisted trace along the boundary divisors.

items.name: Definitions 3.9.1 and 3.9.2: correspondences and cohomological correspondences
items.statement: Definition 3.9.1. A correspondence C over X and Y is a diagram X ←^{p_2} C →^{p_1} Y of S-morphisms, where X, Y, C have the same pure relative dimension over S and p_1, p_2 are projectively embeddable. Definition 3.9.2. A cohomological correspondence from a coherent 𝓕 on X to a coherent 𝓖 on Y is the data of such a C together with a map T : R(p_1)_*p_2^*𝓕 → 𝓖, equivalently by adjunction p_2^*𝓕 → p_1^!𝓖; it induces a map RΓ(X,𝓕) → RΓ(Y,𝓖). Remark 3.9.4 notes that compatibility of the double coset action with the product in the Hecke algebra is easy over Q_p but requires more work over Z_p.

items.name: Theorem 3.9.6 and the Cousin complex: Kempf's vanishing criterion
items.statement: Theorem 3.9.6 (Kempf). Let X be a Noetherian scheme with a filtration Z by closed subschemes such that codim_X(Z_i) ≥ i and Z_i \ Z_{i+1} → X is affine for all i. Then for a maximal Cohen–Macaulay coherent sheaf 𝓕 on X the Cousin complex Cous_Z(𝓕) is quasi-isomorphic to 𝓕. Remark 3.9.7: if each Z_i \ Z_{i+1} is affine then Cous_Z(𝓕) is a complex of acyclic sheaves. Example 3.9.9 computes the Ext-sheaves in the case of effective Cartier divisors meeting properly, through the twisted Koszul complex.

items.name: Propositions 3.9.11 and 3.9.15: the Hecke action on the coherent cohomology of the compactification
items.statement: Proposition 3.9.11. RΓ(X_n, ω^κ(−D)) is computed by Γ(X_n, Cous_Z(ω^κ(−D))) for the stratification Z by the boundary. Lemma 3.9.12 gives an injection of that Cousin complex into the one over Y_n, Lemma 3.9.13 that a cohomological correspondence induces one of Cousin complexes compatible with the augmentation, and Proposition 3.9.15 concludes that the prime-to-p Hecke algebra 𝓗^p acts on RΓ(X^{G_1},ω^κ(−D)) and on RΓ(X^{G_1},ω^κ). Remark 3.9.16 extends this to composites over three tame levels and three cone decompositions.

items.name: Lemmas 3.9.18 and 3.9.22: the normalized Hecke operators T_{w,1} and T_w at w|p
items.statement: The Siegel and Klingen correspondences at w|p give cohomological correspondences on ω^κ which are divisible by explicit powers of p: Lemma 3.9.18 shows the Siegel one is divisible by p^3 when l_w ≥ 2, and Lemma 3.9.22 that the two Klingen maps Θ_1 and Θ_2 are divisible by p^{2+l_w} and p respectively. The resulting normalized operators are written T_{w,1} and T_w. Remark 3.9.19 records that the correspondence defining T_{w,1} is the double coset [GSp_4(O_{F_w})diag(1,1,p^{−1},p^{−1})GSp_4(O_{F_w})], which differs from the spherical operator by a central element, and Remark 3.9.21 gives the double coset formula for T_w as a product of two Klingen cosets. Remark 3.9.23: the actions are independent of the compactification.

items.name: Theorem 3.10.1: coherent cohomology in terms of automorphic forms
items.statement: Theorem 3.10.1. Let κ = (k_v,l_v)_{v|∞} with k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 2, k_v ≡ l_v mod 2, and let m be non-Eisenstein. (1) For i = 0, 1 there is a GSp_4(A_F^∞)//K-equivariant inclusion ⊕_π (π^∞)_m^K ⊗ Ē ⊆ H^i(X_K^{G_1},ω^κ(−D))_m^{|·|^2} ⊗ Ē, the sum being over the cuspidal automorphic representations of the appropriate weight and central character occurring in degree i. (2) Under a regularity assumption on κ this inclusion is an equality in degrees 0 and 1. Corollary 3.10.5: in that case dim H^1 = l_0·dim H^0 where l_0 is the number of infinite places v with l_v = 2. Lemma 3.10.7 is the vanishing H^0(D,ω^κ)_m ⊗ Ē = 0 of the boundary cohomology at a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal.

items.name: §4: higher Hida theory for GSp_4 over a totally real field
items.statement: Classical Hida theory for GSp_4 gives a projective module over the 2[F:Q]-dimensional weight space. Higher Hida theory, constructed for F = Q by Pilloni, gives instead a perfect complex of amplitude [0,1] over a one-dimensional hyperplane of the weight space, obtained by working over the complement of the supersingular locus (the p-rank ≥ 1 stratum), which is not affine but whose image in the minimal compactification has cohomological dimension one. This section constructs all the intermediate theories for p split completely in F, allowing the weight space at each v|p to be one- or two-dimensional; the one theorem used later is Theorem 4.6.1.

items.name: §4.1: Hasse invariants and the p-rank stratification
items.statement: For K_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v)} the p-divisible group 𝓖_v over X carries a (possibly degree p^2) quasi-polarization, and Ha(𝓖_v) ∈ H^0(X_1, det ω_{𝓖,v}^{p−1}) is its Hasse invariant, compatible with étale isogenies and with duality. Its non-vanishing locus X_1^{≥_v 2} = X_1^{=_v 2} is the ordinary locus at v and its vanishing locus X_1^{≤_v 1}, taken reduced, the non-ordinary locus. There is a secondary Hasse invariant Ha'(𝓖_v) ∈ H^0(X_1^{≤_v1}, det ω_{𝓖,v}^{p^2−1}) whose non-vanishing locus X_1^{=_v1} is the rank one locus and whose vanishing locus X_1^{=_v0}, non-reduced, is the supersingular locus. Intersecting over disjoint sets of places gives the strata X_1^{*(i)_{I_i}a_i}, which are Cohen–Macaulay and indeed local complete intersections over F_p, and everything descends to X_1^{G_1}.

items.name: §4.1: density of the ordinary and rank one loci
items.statement: For K_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v), Kli(v), Si(v), Iw(v)} at one place v and hyperspecial or paramodular elsewhere, the space |X_{K,1}^{*(i)_{I_i}a_i, =_v 2}| is dense in |X_{K,1}^{*(i)_{I_i}a_i}|, and if K_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v), Kli(v)} then |X_{K,1}^{*(i)_{I_i}a_i,=_v1}| is dense in |X_{K,1}^{*(i)_{I_i}a_i,≤_v1}|. It suffices to check the first for K_v = Iw(v) and the second for K_v = Kli(v), and then to check the corresponding statement for the local models, the first being in Faltings–Chai and the second following from the Kottwitz–Rapoport stratification at Iwahori level and its image at Klingen level.

items.name: Theorem 4.2.1: the vanishing theorem for Klingen ordinary cohomology
items.statement: Theorem 4.2.1. Put T^I = ∏_{w∈I}T_w ∏_{w∈I^c}T_{w,1}. There is a universal constant C depending only on p and F, not on the tame level K^p, such that if l_w ≥ 2 for all w, k_w − l_w ≥ C for all w ∈ I and l_w ≥ C for all w ∈ I^c, then RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I},ω^κ(−D)) carries a locally finite action of T^I and its ordinary part e(T^I)RΓ is a perfect complex concentrated in degrees [0,#I]. Remark 4.2.2 notes that with explicit bounds one can prove local finiteness for the individual Hecke operators.

items.name: Theorems 4.2.4 and 4.2.13: the Siegel operator and the ordinary locus
items.statement: Theorem 4.2.4. There is a universal constant C such that for J ⊆ S_p with l_w ≥ C for all w ∈ J, the complex RΓ(X_1^{G_1,≥_J2},ω^κ) has a locally finite action of T^J = ∏_{w∈J}T_{w,1} and e(T^J)RΓ(X_1^{G_1},ω^κ) → e(T^J)RΓ(X_1^{G_1,≥_J2},ω^κ) is a quasi-isomorphism. Theorem 4.2.13 is the strengthening actually used, allowing a further disjoint set I_a of places on whose rank ≤ 1 locus one works. The proofs go through Lemmas 4.2.6–4.2.10: the étale part of the Siegel correspondence commutes with the Hasse invariant, Ha(𝓖_w) is not a zero divisor on the relevant strata because they are Cohen–Macaulay and the non-ordinary loci have codimension one, the correspondence restricts to the non-ordinary locus, and there the restricted correspondence vanishes for l_w large.

items.name: Theorem 4.2.12 and Corollaries 4.2.26 and 4.2.29: the Klingen operator and the rank one locus
items.statement: Theorem 4.2.12. For pairwise disjoint I_a, I_b, J ⊆ S_p and T^{I_b,J} = ∏_{w∈I_b}T_w ∏_{w∈J}T_{w,1} there is a universal constant C such that if k_w − l_w ≥ C and l_w ≥ 2 for w ∈ I_b and l_w ≥ C for w ∈ J then RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I_{a,b},J},ω^κ) carries a locally finite action of T^{I_b,J} whose ordinary part is a perfect complex in the expected degrees. The proof uses Lemmas 4.2.14, 4.2.15, 4.2.19, 4.2.20, 4.2.22 and 4.2.23: the two halves T'_w and T''_w of the Klingen correspondence commute with Ha and with the secondary Hasse invariant Ha', T_w = T'_{w,et}∘T''_{w,et} on the rank one locus, and T'_w vanishes on the supersingular locus when k_w − l_w is large. Corollaries 4.2.16, 4.2.21, 4.2.24, 4.2.25, 4.2.26 and 4.2.29 assemble these into local finiteness, perfectness and the quasi-isomorphisms between ordinary cohomology on the various strata.

items.name: §4.3: the Igusa tower at Klingen level and the p-adic sheaves Ω^κ
items.statement: Writing 𝔛_K for the p-adic formal completion of X_K and 𝔛_K^{≥1} ⊂ 𝔛_K for the rank ≥ 1 locus, the formal scheme 𝔛^{≥1}_{K,Kli}(p^m) → 𝔛_K^{≥1} parametrizes subgroups H_m ⊂ 𝓖[p^m] étale-locally isomorphic to μ_{p^m} ⊗ O_F, equivalently H_m = ∏_{w|p}H_{m,w} with H_{m,w} ⊂ 𝓖_w[p^m] isomorphic to μ_{p^m}. Proposition 4.3.3: this morphism is affine and étale, and finite étale over the ordinary locus 𝔛_K^{≥2}. Passing to the limit gives 𝔛^{≥1}_{K,Kli}(p^∞). Lemma 4.3.8 gives, via the Hodge–Tate map, a canonical isomorphism identifying the relevant tensor product of ω_{H_∞,v} and ω_{𝓖_v/H_{∞,v}} with a sheaf Ω^κ, and Corollary 4.3.9 a canonical surjection ω^κ|_{𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞)} → Ω^κ = Ω^{κ̃_I} ⊗_{Λ̃_I,κ} Z_p.

items.name: §4.4: the weight space Λ_I, the descent character d, and the p-adic forms M_I^{pad,κ_I}
items.statement: For p ≠ 2 and I ⊆ S_p, T_I is the relevant torus, T_I = T_I^f × T_I^0 with T_I^0 pro-p, and Λ_I = Z_p⟦T_I^0⟧. A classical algebraic weight κ = ((k_v,2)_{v∈I},(k_v,l_v)_{v∈I^c}) with k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 mod (p−1) gives a Z_p-point of Spf Λ_I through the character ∏_{v∈I}x_v^{k_v−2}∏_{v∈I^c}x_v^{k_v−2}y_v^{l_v−2}. The group (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)} embeds diagonally in T_I, and since p > 2 one may define the descent character d(x) = √(x_0) ∈ Λ_I^×, which lifts the twisting action on Ω^{κ_I} and gives the quotient 𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli}(p^n). One sets M_I^{pad,κ_I} = RΓ(𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli}(p^∞), Ω^{κ_I}(−D)), the cohomology of p-adic cuspidal modular forms of weight κ_I, and Proposition 4.4.3 shows the canonical map to the cohomology over 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞) is split in the derived category of Z_p-modules.

items.name: §4.5: the Hecke operators U_{Kli(v),1}, U_{v,1} and U_{v,2} on p-adic modular forms
items.statement: On the cohomology of the p-adic sheaves over the Igusa tower one constructs the operators U_{w,1} (the usual U_p at w, Remark 4.5.3) and U_{w,2}, together with U_{Kli(w),1} for w ∈ I, each through a correspondence of formal schemes and a normalized trace map: Lemma 4.5.4 gives p^{−3}Tr_{u_1}, Lemma 4.5.10 gives p^{−2}Tr_{r_1} and Lemma 4.5.13 gives p^{−1}Tr_{s_2}, each proved by a Serre–Tate computation of the map on top differentials; Lemma 4.5.9 shows the relevant formal subscheme is open and closed in the fibre product. Lemma 4.5.15: the operators {U_{Kli(v),1},U_{v,2}}_{v∈I} and {U_{v,1},U_{v,2}}_{v∈I^c} commute on RΓ(𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli(p^∞)},Ω^{κ_I}(−D)). Lemma 4.5.17: for w ∈ I one has the quadratic relation U_{Iw(w),1}(U_{Kli(w),1} − U_{Iw(w),1}) = U_{w,2} on the ordinary locus at w.

items.name: Theorem 4.6.1: the perfect Hida complex M_I
items.statement: Theorem 4.6.1. (1) The operator U^I = ∏_{w|p}U_{w,2}∏_{w∈I^c}U_{w,1} is locally finite on M_I^{pad,κ_I}. (2) With e(U^I) the associated ordinary projector and M_I := e(U^I)M_I^{pad,κ_I}, the complex M_I is a perfect complex of Λ_I-modules concentrated in the interval [0,#I]. (3) For every classical algebraic weight κ in the appropriate congruence class there is a canonical isomorphism comparing the specialization of M_I with the ordinary part of the classical coherent cohomology. This is the only theorem of §4 used later in the paper.

items.name: Lemmas 4.6.3–4.6.27: the comparison of T-ordinary and U-ordinary cohomology
items.statement: The proof of Theorem 4.6.1 compares the classical operators T_{w,1}, T_w with the p-adic operators U_{w,1}, U_{w,2}. Lemmas 4.6.3, 4.6.4, 4.6.6 and 4.6.7 show that the U-correspondences commute with the Hasse invariant and the secondary Hasse invariant and that Ha is not a zero divisor on them. Proposition 4.6.9 shows U^I is locally finite on the relevant H^0 and that the ordinarity condition prevents newforms of Klingen level (Remark 4.6.10). Lemma 4.6.12 gives T̃_w = T_w and U_{w,2}T̃''_w = U_{w,2}^2; Lemmas 4.6.13 and 4.6.14 that the canonical map intertwines T_w with U_{w,2} and T_{w,1} with U_{w,1} on the rank one locus; Corollary 4.6.15, Lemma 4.6.16 and Lemma 4.6.17 give the congruence Tr∘(∏U_{w,2})^n∘ι ≡ p^{#J^c}(∏T̃_w)^n mod p^{inf(k_w−l_w)} and hence that the ordinary projectors agree when k_w − l_w > p^{#J^c}. Proposition 4.6.19, Lemmas 4.6.21, 4.6.23, 4.6.24, 4.6.25, 4.6.26 and 4.6.27 pass from level Kli(p) to Kli(p^∞) and prove perfectness, using Lemma 4.6.22, a Nakayama criterion: a bounded complex of m-adically complete flat R-modules whose reduction has finite-dimensional cohomology in degrees [a,b] is perfect and concentrated there.

items.name: §5: the doubling phenomenon and the operator Z_w
items.statement: Doubling embeds two copies of the space of Klingen ordinary modular forms into the space of Iwahori ordinary forms through the two degeneracy maps, so that the associated Galois representation is Iwahori ordinary in two ways, with α_w and β_w as unramified subspaces; the genericity assumption ᾱ_w ≠ β̄_w then forces a two-dimensional unramified summand. Earlier incarnations of doubling rested on the q-expansion principle; here the argument is geometric and rests on analysing the Hecke operator Z_w = U_{Kli(w),1} − U_{Iw(w),1} along the w-non-ordinary locus. The model case of GL_2/Q is recalled in §5.1.

items.name: Lemmas 5.3.1, 5.3.2 and 5.4.1: the operators U_{Kli(w),1}, U_{Iw(w),1} and Z_w are p-integral
items.statement: Lemma 5.3.1. R(v_1)_*O_{𝔠_{Kli(w),1}} = (v_1)_*O and there is a trace map to O_{𝔛^I}. Lemma 5.3.2: the resulting cohomological correspondence U_{Kli(w),1} : (Rv_1)_*v_2^*ω^κ → ω^κ is p-integral. Lemma 5.4.1: the cohomological correspondences U_{Iw(w),1} and Z_w are p-integral. Over the ordinary locus at w one has the identities U_{Kli(w),1} = U_{Iw(w),1} + p^{l_w−2}Z_w and, from Lemma 4.5.17, U_{Iw(w),1}Z_w = U_{w,2}.

items.name: §5.5: the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism and its compatibilities
items.statement: Proposition 5.5.1: for a prime-to-p quasi-isogeny φ : A → A' of tuples with φιφ^{−1} = ι' and φ^tλ'φ = xλ, the Kodaira–Spencer maps det(ω_A)^3 → K and det(ω_{A'})^3 → K fit in a commutative diagram with the explicit twist by x. Proposition 5.5.2: the Kodaira–Spencer map is compatible with base change along a finite flat map of smooth S-schemes of relative dimension 3[F:Q]. Proposition 5.5.3: over 𝔜^I the Kodaira–Spencer map ω^3 → K_{𝔜^I/Z_p} is an isomorphism.

items.name: Definition 5.6.2 and Proposition 5.6.3: the partial Frobenius F_w
items.statement: Definition 5.6.2. For a point (A,ι,λ,{H_v},η) of Y_1^I one sets L_w = ker(F : A[w^∞] → A[w^∞]^{(p)}), a maximal isotropic subgroup of A[w], and defines the partial Frobenius F_w : Y_1^I → Y_1^I by quotienting by L_w. Proposition 5.6.3: F_w is finite flat of degree p^3, and restricts to a finite flat map of degree p^2 on Y_1^{I,=_w1}.

items.name: Propositions 5.6.1, 5.6.4, 5.6.5 and 5.6.7: U_{Iw(w),1} and the trace along the rank one locus
items.statement: Proposition 5.6.1 reduces the Kodaira–Spencer comparison for the Klingen correspondence modulo p. Proposition 5.6.4: the map Ha_w·U_{Iw(w),1} : F_{w,*}ω^2 → ω^2 ⊗ ω_w^{p−1} on Y_1^{I,=_w2} extends to Y_1^I and is identified under Kodaira–Spencer with an explicit map of dualizing sheaves. Proposition 5.6.5 records the compatibility of that map with restriction to the rank one locus, and Proposition 5.6.7 the resulting commutative square relating Ha_w·U_{Iw(w),1} on H^0(Y_1^I,ω^2) with an explicit map γ_1 on H^0(Y_1^{I,=_w1},·).

items.name: §5.7: U_{w,2} is the square of the partial Frobenius on the rank one locus
items.statement: Lemma 5.7.1 puts the correspondence 𝔠^I_{w,2} in a Cartesian diagram over the w-spherical space, and Lemma 5.7.2 shows p_1 is finite flat of degree p^4. Proposition 5.7.3: the restriction of p_2 to p_2^{−1}(Y_1^{I,=_w1}) is an isomorphism onto Y_1^{I,=_w1}, and under this identification p_1 becomes F_w^2. Proposition 5.7.4: the map δ_0 is divisible by p, δ = p^{−1}δ_0 : p_2^*ω_w → p_1^*ω_w is an isomorphism, and under δ^{p−1} one has p_1^*Ha_w = p_2^*Ha_w. Propositions 5.7.5, 5.7.6, 5.7.8 and 5.7.9 then identify U_{w,2} on H^0(Y_1^I,ω^2) with the composite γ_2∘γ_1 on the rank one locus through the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism.

items.name: Lemmas 5.8.1, 5.8.2 and 5.8.3: the doubling map and its equivariance
items.statement: Lemma 5.8.1: on H^0(X_1^{I,=_w2},ω^2(−D)) one has U_{Iw(w),1}Z_w = U_{w,2}. The doubling map is the sum of the two degeneracy maps H^0(X_1^I,ω^2(−D))^{⊕2} → H^0(X_1^{I,=_w2},ω^2(−D)). Lemma 5.8.2: it is equivariant for U_{Iw(w),1}, and U_{Iw(w),1} on the source commutes with U_{w,2}. Lemma 5.8.3: the image of the U_{w,2}-ordinary part lands in the e(U_{Iw(w),1}U_{w,2})-part, on which U_{Iw(w),1} is invertible.

items.name: Theorems 5.8.4 and 5.8.6: the main doubling results
items.statement: Theorem 5.8.4. Suppose w ∈ I and f ∈ H^0(X_1^{G_1,I},ω^2(−D)) satisfies U_{Kli(w),1}f = (α_w+β_w)f, U_{Iw(w),1}f = α_wf and U_{w,2}f = α_wβ_wf with α_w, β_w ≠ 0. Then f = 0. Theorem 5.8.6 (Doubling). The doubling map e(U_{w,2})H^0(X_1^{G_1,I},ω^2(−D))^{⊕2} → e(U_{Iw(w),1}U_{w,2})H^0(X_1^{G_1,I,=_w2},ω^2(−D)) is injective. Remark 5.8.5 records the stronger statement that U_{w,2}f ≠ 0 implies U_{Iw(w),1}f does not extend, and Remark 5.8.7 puts Theorem 5.8.6 in the generalized-eigenspace form used in §7.9.

items.name: §5.9: vanishing in partial negative weight and the Fourier–Jacobi expansion
items.statement: Proposition 5.9.1. For w ∈ I, p > 3 and [F:Q] > 1 one has H^0(X_{K_p(I)K^p,1}^I, ω^2 ⊗ ω_w^{1−p}) = 0. The section says explicitly that this partially strengthens Corollary 5.4.5 but is not needed in the paper; it is the vanishing that would give the strengthening of the doubling theorem announced in Remark 5.8.5. The proof uses Proposition 5.9.3, a Fourier–Jacobi expansion principle giving a natural injection of H^0 of the cuspidal sheaf into a product of H^0(A_1^I, ω^2 ⊗ ω_v^{1−p} ⊗ 𝓛_ξ) over ξ in the totally positive part of a fractional ideal; Lemma 5.9.4, that for an abelian scheme A/S and a rigidified invertible sheaf 𝓛 the restriction 𝓛^{n^3}|_{A[n]} is trivial; and Proposition 5.9.5, the vanishing of H^0 in weights with some k_w < 0. Remark 5.9.2 records that the cases p = 3 and F = Q are only sketched, because the required properties of Fourier–Jacobi expansions could not be found in the literature.

items.name: §6: higher Coleman theory for Hilbert–Siegel modular forms
items.statement: The purpose of §6 is a classicality theorem in characteristic zero for the H^0 of the Hida complexes and the proof that those complexes are balanced, that is have Euler characteristic zero. The method is an interplay between three objects: the complex of classical forms, the complex of overconvergent locally analytic forms on the adic generic fibre, and the complex of Klingen ordinary forms. It is the analogue for GSp_4 over a totally real field of Coleman's classicality theorem and of the overconvergent theory of Andreatta–Iovita–Pilloni.

items.name: Theorem 6.1.3: cohomology of a projective formal scheme with an affine analytic model
items.statement: Theorem 6.1.3. Let 𝔖 be an admissible formal scheme admitting a projective map 𝔖 → 𝔖' to an affine admissible formal scheme inducing an isomorphism of the associated analytic adic spaces over Spa(C_p,O_{C_p}), and let 𝔉 be an admissible sheaf on it. Then the cohomology of 𝔉 is computed after inverting p by the global sections, so that the analytic cohomology is concentrated in degree zero on such a piece.

items.name: §6.1: the canonical filtration, the modified sheaf of differentials and the sheaves 𝔊^{κ_A,w}
items.statement: On the adic spaces 𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε) defined by bounds on the degrees of the canonical subgroups, Lemma 6.1.5 shows that Fil_v^{can} is a locally free O/p^{ε_v}-module of rank one and locally a direct factor in ω^{mod}_{𝓖_v}/p^{ε_v}, where ω^{mod} is the modified integral lattice supplied by the Hodge–Tate map. From an analytic character κ_A of the torus one builds the quasi-coherent sheaves 𝔊^{κ_A,w} of w-analytic functions on the relevant torsor; Lemma 6.1.11 shows 𝔊^{κ_A,w}/p^{inf w_v} is an inductive limit of coherent extensions of the structure sheaf and Lemma 6.1.12 that 𝔊^{κ_A,w}/p is flat.

items.name: Theorem 6.2.6 and Proposition 6.2.5: the vanishing theorem on the minimal compactification
items.statement: Remark 6.2.2 explains that the determinant of the Hodge–Tate map factors through ⊗_{v|p}Λ^2(O_{F_v}/p^n)^4. Lemma 6.2.3: there is a projective map 𝔛^*_{K(p^n)}(ε,(i_v)) → 𝔛^{*-HT}_{K(p^n)}(ε,(i_v)) which is an isomorphism on analytic adic spaces, the target being an affine formal scheme. Proposition 6.2.5: R^iπ_*O_{𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε)}(−D) = 0 for i > 0. Theorem 6.2.6: for ε ∈ Q_{>0}^{S_p} and n with inf_v n_v ≥ sup_v n(ε_v), the complex RΓ(𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε), 𝔊^{κ_A,w} ⊗ (det ω^{mod}_𝓖)^2(−D))[1/p] has cohomology concentrated in degrees [0,#I].

items.name: §6.3: the complex of overconvergent locally analytic cuspidal forms and its compactness
items.statement: Lemma 6.3.2 identifies the flag varieties 𝓕𝓛 at level K(p^n) as base changes from level K(I,p^n). Proposition 6.3.6: the complex C_{cusp}(n,ε,w,κ_A ⊗ (2,2)) is represented by a bounded complex of projective Banach A[1/p]-modules, by a Čech argument. Proposition 6.3.7: its cohomology vanishes outside degrees [0,#I], by Theorem 6.2.6. After descent along the character one obtains the overconvergent complex for G_1. Lemma 6.3.13 shows the image of u_2 lands in the smaller neighbourhood, and Lemma 6.3.14 that the operator U^I is compact on C_{cusp}(G_1,n,ε,w,κ_A ⊗ (2,2)) and factors through the restriction maps, which is what makes the Fredholm theory apply. Remark 6.3.10 records that for v ∈ I^c the operator U_{v,2} alone does not improve analyticity, but the composite U_{v,1}U_{v,2} does.

items.name: Theorem 6.3.16: local constancy of the Euler characteristic in the weight
items.statement: Theorem 6.3.16. The map W_{cl} → Z sending κ to Σ_i(−1)^i dim e(U^I)H^i_{cusp}(G_1,†,κ) is locally constant. Remark 6.3.17 notes that for #I = 1 this says that dim H^0 − dim H^1 of the ordinary overconvergent cohomology is locally constant in the weight, which is what reduces the comparison of ordinary and overconvergent cohomology to the regular weight case.

items.name: Proposition 6.4.1 and Proposition 6.4.2: slope bounds and the analytic BGG resolution
items.statement: Proposition 6.4.1. On H^i_{cusp}(G_1,†,κ) the slopes of (U_{v,1})_{v∈I^c} and (U_{v,2})_{v|p} are ≥ −3, and on H^0 they are ≥ 0. Proposition 6.4.2: for a dominant algebraic weight κ = ((k_v,l_v)) with l_v = 2 for v ∈ I and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 mod (p−1), there is a relative analytic BGG resolution 0 → ω^κ(−D) → 𝓕^{κ,w^-} ⊗ (det ω_𝓖)^2(−D) → ⊕_{s}… resolving the classical sheaf by the analytic ones indexed by the Weyl elements. Corollary 6.4.3 deduces from it the bound on the slopes for which the comparison map on cohomology is an isomorphism.

items.name: Theorem 6.5.8: the classicality theorem
items.statement: Theorem 6.5.8. The canonical map RΓ(𝓧^{G_1}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D))[U_{v,2} < k_v+l_v−3 for v ∈ I, U_{v,1} < l_v−3 for v ∈ I^c] → RΓ(𝓧^{G_1,mult,†}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D)) with the same slope conditions is a quasi-isomorphism; the bracket means the part of slope less than the indicated bound for the indicated operator. Lemma 6.5.4 gives the action and compactness of U_{v,1}, U_{v,2} on the classical sheaves over the relevant neighbourhoods, and Lemma 6.5.6 that the ordinary multiplicative overconvergent complex is perfect and supported in degrees [0,#I]. Remark 6.5.10 records that for I = ∅ and H^0 this is the theorem of Bijakowski.

items.name: §6.5: the dynamics of the Hecke correspondences and analytic continuation of finite slope forms
items.statement: Lemmas 6.5.12 and 6.5.13 compute the effect of the Hecke correspondence C^{(1)}_w on the degrees deg H_v and deg L_v of the level subgroups for w ∈ I and w ∈ I^c respectively. Corollaries 6.5.14 and 6.5.15 deduce that a power of U_{w,1} (resp. U_{w,2}) contracts the neighbourhoods 𝓧(J) towards the multiplicative locus. Lemmas 6.5.17, 6.5.18, 6.5.19 and 6.5.20 give the actions on cohomology and the isomorphisms on finite slope parts under shrinking the neighbourhood. Proposition 6.5.22 and Corollary 6.5.23 give the factorization of U_{w,1}^n through a truncated sheaf and hence an extension map on the part killed by a polynomial whose roots have valuation < l_w − 3; Proposition 6.5.24 and Corollary 6.5.25 are the corresponding statements for U_{w,2} with the bound k_w + l_w − 3. Lemmas 6.5.27 and 6.5.28 assemble them into the statement that restriction is an isomorphism on finite slope parts.

items.name: Propositions 6.6.1 and 6.6.2 and Theorems 6.6.4 and 6.6.5: ordinary cohomology is overconvergent, and ordinary classicality
items.statement: Proposition 6.6.1. For #I = 1 and classical algebraic weights κ with l_v = 2 for v ∈ I and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 mod (p−1), the restriction map e(U^I)RΓ(𝓧^{G_1,mult,†}_{K_p(I)K^p},ω^κ(−D)) → M_I ⊗^L_{Λ_I,κ}C_p is a map whose behaviour is controlled by Euler characteristics. Proposition 6.6.2: for #I ≤ 1 the two sides have the same Euler characteristic, using Proposition 2.4.26 (Remark 6.6.3 points out the subtlety in applying it). Theorem 6.6.4: for #I ≤ 1 and classical algebraic κ with l_v = 2 for v ∈ I there is a canonical isomorphism e(U^I)RΓ(𝓧^{G_1,mult,†},ω^κ(−D)) = M_I ⊗^L_{Λ_I,κ}C_p. Theorem 6.6.5 (ordinary classicity): for #I ≤ 1 and κ classical algebraic with l_v = 2 if v ∈ I and l_v ≥ 4 otherwise, the canonical map e(U^I)RΓ(X^{G_1}_{K_p(I)K^p},ω^κ(−D))[1/p] → M_I ⊗^L_{Λ_I,κ}Q_p is a quasi-isomorphism.

items.name: Definitions 7.1.2, 7.1.4 and 7.1.5: lifts, local and global deformation problems for GSp_4
items.statement: Definition 7.1.2. A lift of ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is a continuous ρ : G_{F_v} → GSp_4(A) to a CNL_{Λ_v}-algebra A with ρ mod m_A = ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} and ν∘ρ = ψ|_{G_{F_v}}; 𝓓_v^□ is the functor of lifts, represented by R_v^□. Definition 7.1.4. A local deformation problem is a subfunctor 𝓓_v of 𝓓_v^□ represented by a quotient R_v of R_v^□ and stable under conjugation by ker(GSp_4(A) → GSp_4(k)). Definition 7.1.5. A global deformation problem is a tuple 𝓢 = (ρ̄, S, {Λ_v}_{v∈S}, ψ, {𝓓_v}_{v∈S}) with ρ̄ : G_{F,S} → GSp_4(k), ψ : G_{F,S} → Λ^× lifting ν∘ρ̄ and 𝓓_v a local deformation problem at each v ∈ S. Remark 7.1.1: Λ_v = O for v ∤ p, and an Iwasawa algebra for v|p. Lemma 7.1.6 relates the framed and unframed deformation rings by R_𝓢^T ≅ R_𝓢 ⊗̂_Λ 𝓣.

items.name: Lemma 7.1.3: pure points of the unrestricted local deformation ring away from p are smooth
items.statement: Lemma 7.1.3. For v ∤ p a closed point x of the generic fibre of R_v^□ is smooth if and only if (ad^0ρ_x)(1)^{G_{F_v}} = 0; in particular if ρ_x is pure then x is smooth, since purity forces Hom(ρ_x, ρ_x(1)) = 0.

items.name: Proposition 7.2.1: the global presentation over the local deformation rings
items.statement: Proposition 7.2.1. Let T ⊇ S_p and suppose Λ_v = O and 𝓓_v = 𝓓_v^□ for v ∈ S \ T. Then there is a local Λ-algebra surjection R_𝓢^{T,loc}⟦X_1,…,X_g⟧ → R_𝓢^T with g = h^1_{𝓢^⊥,T}(ad^0ρ̄(1)) − Σ_{v∈T}h^0(F_v,ad^0ρ̄) + h^0(F,ad^0ρ̄) + Σ_{v|∞}h^0(F_v,ad^0ρ̄) − #T·dim ad^0, the standard Galois-cohomological count in the GSp_4 setting.

items.name: Definition 7.3.1: p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary representations
items.statement: Definition 7.3.1. ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary if it is conjugate to a representation with diagonal blocks λ_{ᾱ_v}, λ_{β̄_v}, ε̄^{−1}λ_{β̄_v}^{−1}, ε̄^{−1}λ_{ᾱ_v}^{−1} in the displayed block upper triangular shape, with ᾱ_v ≠ β̄_v. Remark 7.3.2 explains the terminology and the alternatives considered; Remark 7.3.3 notes that a stronger p-distinguishedness hypothesis, as in Calegari–Geraghty for GSp_4, would suffice for potential modularity but the weaker one greatly widens the applicability to actual modularity.

items.name: Proposition 7.3.4 and Proposition 7.3.16: the ordinary local deformation rings at v|p
items.statement: Proposition 7.3.4. The generic fibres R_v^{B,ᾱβ̄_v}[1/p] and R_v^P[1/p] are irreducible, of relative dimensions 16 and 14 over Q_p. Proposition 7.3.16: for ρ̄ p-distinguished, R^{P,univ} and R^P are complete intersections, connected in characteristic zero, with non-smooth locus of codimension at least two in characteristic zero, so that their generic fibres are irreducible of the stated dimension. Remark 7.3.17 notes that the argument establishes the complete intersection property but not the expected flatness over O. Definition 7.3.11 introduces the subfunctors 𝓓^{B,tri} and 𝓓^{P,tri} of deformations landing in B or P with the framing in the upper right corner, and Lemma 7.3.12 shows R^{B,□} is formally smooth over R^{B,tri} of relative dimension 4. Lemma 7.3.15 gives R^{P,tri} ≅ (R_A ⊗̂_Λ R_B) ⊗̂_{R^{GL_1×GL_1}} R_{AB}, with R^P formally smooth over it of relative dimension 5.

items.name: Lemmas 7.3.6, 7.3.7, 7.3.9 and 7.3.14: the ordinary deformation rings for GL_2 and the H^2 computation
items.statement: Lemma 7.3.6. The generic fibre R^{B_2}[1/p] of the Borel-ordinary GL_2 deformation ring is irreducible of relative dimension 5 over Q_p. Lemma 7.3.7 gives explicit presentations of R^{B_2,tri} as an R^{GL_1}-algebra in each of the cases distinguished by whether γ^2 = 1 and whether the relevant extension class vanishes, showing it is a complete intersection, flat over Λ and irreducible of relative dimension 4 over O; Remark 7.3.8 records why Böckle's descriptions are not in the required form. Lemma 7.3.9: the points of R^{B_2}[1/p] which are non-smooth over Λ are, up to unramified twist, crystalline extensions of ε^{−1} by 1. Lemma 7.3.14 computes when H^2(Q_p, ad^0_B(ρ̄)) is nonzero, in terms of the vanishing of the classes η_{αβ}, η_{α^2}, η_{β^2} and the conditions ᾱ^2 = 1 or β̄^2 = 1.

items.name: Lemma 7.3.18: pure points of the ordinary local deformation rings are smooth
items.statement: Lemma 7.3.18. If x is a closed point of the generic fibre of R_v^{B,ᾱβ̄_v}[1/p] or of R_v^P[1/p] which is pure, then x is smooth.

items.name: Proposition 7.4.2: unrestricted deformation rings at v ∤ p with vanishing H^0(ad^0(1))
items.statement: Proposition 7.4.2. If H^0(F_v, ad^0ρ̄(1)) = 0 then R_v^□ is a power series ring over O in 10 variables; if moreover ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is unramified then so are all of its lifts.

items.name: Lemma 7.4.4: the Taylor–Wiles local condition at an auxiliary prime
items.statement: Lemma 7.4.4. At a Taylor–Wiles prime, any lift ρ : G_{F_v} → GSp_4(A) of ρ̄ is GSp_4(A)-conjugate to γ_1 ⊕ γ_2 ⊕ ψγ_2^{−1} ⊕ ψγ_1^{−1} for unique continuous characters γ_i : G_{F_v} → A^× reducing to the prescribed unramified characters.

items.name: Propositions 7.4.7 and 7.4.8 and Lemma 7.4.6: Ihara avoidance deformation rings for GSp_4
items.statement: For ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} trivial at a place v with q_v ≡ 1 mod p, one considers the deformation rings R_v^χ with tame inertia acting by a fixed pair of characters (χ_1,χ_2). Lemma 7.4.6: if χ_1, χ_2 ≠ 1 and χ_1 ≠ χ_2^{±1} then every closed point of Spec R_v^χ[1/p] is smooth. Proposition 7.4.7: for χ_1 = χ_2 = 1, Spec R_v^1 is equidimensional of dimension 11, every generic point has characteristic zero, every generic point of Spec R_v^1/(λ) is the specialization of a unique generic point of Spec R_v^1, and the further properties needed for Taylor's argument hold. Proposition 7.4.8: for χ_1, χ_2 ≠ 1 and χ_1 ≠ χ_2^{±1}, Spec R_v^χ is irreducible of dimension 11 with generic point of characteristic zero. This is the GSp_4 analogue of Taylor's Ihara avoidance for GL_n.

items.name: Propositions 7.4.10, 7.4.14, 7.4.16, 7.4.17, 7.4.18, 7.4.20, 7.4.21 and Corollary 7.4.15: nilpotent orbits in GSp_4 and the spaces 𝓝(q), 𝓜(x,y;q)
items.statement: Proposition 7.4.10. The centralizers Z_{GSp_4}(N_i) of the four nilpotent classes are smooth over Spec O with fibres of dimensions 11, 7, 5, 3; each connected component is irreducible with irreducible special fibre, and Z_{GSp_4}(N_i) is irreducible except for i = 2, where it has two components. Remark 7.4.11 records that, unlike for GL_n, these centralizers need not be connected and the universal nilpotent need not be Zariski-locally conjugate to N_i. Proposition 7.4.14: the action makes 𝓝(q)_i a 𝓩_i-torsor over 𝓝_i; Corollary 7.4.15: 𝓝(q)_i is smooth over O with equidimensional fibres of dimension 11, irreducible except for i = 2, which has two components. Proposition 7.4.16 lists the irreducible components of 𝓝(q) and of its special fibre; Proposition 7.4.17 the corresponding properties of the components of 𝓜(1,1;q); Proposition 7.4.18 that Spec R[1/p] is connected for R the complete local ring of 𝓜(x,y;q) at (1,1). Propositions 7.4.20 and 7.4.21 twist to fix the central character and identify R̃_v^χ with the complete local ring of 𝓜(x,y;q_v) at (1,1).

items.name: Definition 7.5.2: enormous and weakly enormous subgroups of GSp_4(k)
items.statement: Definition 7.5.2. A subgroup H ⊂ GSp_4(k) is enormous if (E1) H^1(H, ad^0) = 0 for the ten-dimensional representation ad^0; (E2) H acts absolutely irreducibly in its natural representation, so in particular H^0(H, ad^0) = 0; and (E3) for every simple k[H]-submodule W of ad^0 there is a regular semisimple h ∈ H with an eigenvalue α such that the α-eigenspace projection does not annihilate W. Weakly enormous drops (E1). Lemma 7.5.3: enormousness depends only on the image in PGSp_4(k); Lemma 7.5.14: for p ≥ 11 an absolutely irreducible H satisfies (E1) and (E2) automatically.

items.name: Definitions 7.5.6 and 7.5.11: vast and tidy representations
items.statement: Definition 7.5.6. ρ̄ : G_F → GSp_4(k) is vast if either the image of ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}} is enormous for all sufficiently large N, or that image is weakly enormous for all sufficiently large N together with the further conditions listed there. Definition 7.5.11. A subgroup H ⊂ GSp_4(k) is tidy if there is an h ∈ H with ν(h) ≠ 1 such that no two eigenvalues of h have ratio ν(h) (the eigenvalues need not be distinct); ρ̄ is tidy if its image is. Lemma 7.5.5 gives an N beyond which the image of ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}} is independent of N, so Remark 7.5.7 allows N = 3 when p is unramified in F; Remark 7.5.8: vastness is preserved by twisting.

items.name: Lemma 7.5.9: vanishing of Galois cohomology under the big image hypotheses
items.statement: Lemma 7.5.9. Suppose p ≥ 3 and ρ̄ : G_F → GSp_4(k) is continuous, and fix N ≥ 1. Suppose either that the fixed field L of ad^0ρ̄ does not contain ζ_p, or that ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}} has enormous image. Then H^1(Gal(L(ζ_{p^N})/F), ad^0ρ̄) = 0 and the analogous twisted group vanishes, which is what allows the Chebotarev argument for Taylor–Wiles primes.

items.name: Lemmas 7.5.12, 7.5.13, 7.5.15, 7.5.17, 7.5.18, 7.5.19, 7.5.21, 7.5.22, 7.5.25, 7.5.26, 7.5.27: examples of vast and tidy representations
items.statement: Lemma 7.5.12: an absolutely irreducible H whose centre has order at least 3 is tidy. Lemma 7.5.13: for p ≥ 5, any H containing the subgroup Δ ⊂ GL_2(F_p) × GL_2(F_p) of pairs with equal determinant is tidy. Lemma 7.5.15: for p ≥ 3, Sp_4(F_p) is enormous and GSp_4(F_p) is tidy, so a surjective ρ̄ : G_F → GSp_4(F_p) with similitude ε̄^{−1} is vast and tidy. Lemma 7.5.17 gives a criterion for (E3) through the Asai representation; Lemma 7.5.18 shows SL_2(k) ≀ Z/2 is weakly enormous and enormous for k ≠ F_5; Lemma 7.5.19 treats the exceptional case p = 5; Lemma 7.5.21 lists tidy subgroups of GSp_4(F_3), including GSp_4(F_3) itself and a group of order 3840, whose index two intersections with Sp_4(F_3) are enormous; Lemma 7.5.22 shows inductions from GL_2 over a quadratic extension are vast and tidy under explicit hypotheses, with Remark 7.5.23 weakening them at p = 3; Lemmas 7.5.25, 7.5.26 and 7.5.27 construct the dihedral auxiliary extension and handle the mixed cases used in §10.

items.name: Lemma 7.6.1 and Corollary 7.6.3: the existence of Taylor–Wiles primes
items.statement: Lemma 7.6.1. Assume ρ̄ is vast, p ≥ 3 is unramified in F, ψ = ε^{−1}, and k contains all eigenvalues of all elements of ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}). Let q ≥ h^1(F_S/F, ad^0ρ̄(1)). Then for every N ≥ 1 there is a Taylor–Wiles datum (Q_N, (ᾱ_{v,1},…,ᾱ_{v,4})_{v∈Q_N}) of cardinality q with q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N, with ρ̄(Frob_v) having distinct eigenvalues with the stated ratios, and with the dual Selmer group vanishing. Definition 7.6.2 says ρ̄ is odd if ψ(c_v) = −1 for every complex conjugation, and Corollary 7.6.3 gives the version of the lemma with the explicit local conditions used in the patching.

items.name: Hypothesis 7.7.1 and Hypothesis 7.8.1: the standing hypotheses on ρ̄
items.statement: Hypothesis 7.7.1 lists the conditions on ρ̄ under which the global deformation problems are defined: ρ̄ is vast and tidy; for v ∈ S_p, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary; there is a finite set R of places disjoint from S_p at which ρ̄ is trivial with q_v ≡ 1 mod p and the Ihara avoidance conditions hold; and an auxiliary place v_0. Hypothesis 7.8.1 adds that F is totally real with p ≥ 3 split completely, together with the conditions needed to construct Taylor–Wiles data and the level structures of Definition 7.8.2. Lemma 7.8.3: a level K with K_v = Iw_1(v) at some absolutely unramified place of residue characteristic greater than 5 is neat.
items.locator: Hypotheses 7.7.1 and 7.8.1, Definition 7.8.2 and Lemma 7.8.3 (§§7.7–7.8), Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501

items.name: Lemmas 7.8.5 and 7.8.6: the duality used to define the patched modules
items.statement: Lemma 7.8.5. For Λ ∈ CNL_O and a perfect complex M^• of Λ-modules bounded below by 0, put M = RHom^0_Λ(M^•,Λ). Then M ⊗_Λ k = (H^0(M^• ⊗_Λ k))^*, and when Λ = O the module M is the Pontryagin dual of H^0 of the complex with E/O coefficients. Lemma 7.8.6 is the corresponding statement for a morphism of finite free O-modules. Remark 7.8.7 explains that this reproduces the construction of the patched modules in Calegari–Geraghty as Pontryagin duals of cohomology with E/O coefficients.

items.name: Definition 7.8.8: p-adic weights and the spaces of ordinary p-adic forms M^{χ,I,αβ,Q}
items.statement: Definition 7.8.8. For I ⊆ S_p a weight is a homomorphism κ : Λ_I → O, corresponding to a tuple (θ_{v,1},θ_{v,2})_{v∈S_p} of characters of I_{F_v} with trivial reduction, with θ_{v,1} = θ_{v,2} for v ∈ I; p_κ denotes its kernel. From the higher Hida complexes at the levels of Definition 7.8.2 one forms the modules M^{χ,I,αβ,Q} = RHom^0(M^{•,I}_{K^p_1(Q)}, Λ_I[Δ_Q]) for each choice of Ihara avoidance character χ, each subset I, each choice αβ of ordinary Hecke eigenvalue at each v|p and each Taylor–Wiles datum Q. Remark 7.8.9 fixes a regular weight κ_reg in which Theorems 3.10.1 and 6.6.5 apply.

items.name: Propositions 7.8.10 and 7.8.11: freeness and balancedness over Λ_I[Δ_Q]
items.statement: Proposition 7.8.10. For all v ∈ Q ∪ R the subquotients H_v, L_v/H_v, H_v^⊥/L_v and A[v]/H_v^⊥ of the level structure extend to finite étale k(v)-group schemes of rank 1 over the toroidal compactification at level K_0^p(Q,R), and the map from level K_1^p(Q,R) is finite étale with group Δ_Q. Proposition 7.8.11. M^{χ,∅,αβ,Q} is a finite free Λ_∅[Δ_Q]-module, and if #I = 1 then M^{χ,I,αβ,Q} is a balanced Λ_I[Δ_Q]-module.

items.name: Proposition 7.9.1: doubling as surjections between the modules for I ⊆ I'
items.statement: Proposition 7.9.1 (Doubling). For each choice of αβ and each I ⊆ I' there are natural surjections M^{χ,I,αβ} ⊗_{Λ_I}Λ_{I'} → M^{χ,I',αβ} and M^{χ,I,αβ,Q} ⊗_{Λ_I}Λ_{I'} → M^{χ,I',αβ,Q}. This is the module-theoretic form of Theorem 5.8.6.

items.name: Theorem 7.9.4 and Corollary 7.9.6: Galois representations over the Hecke algebras
items.statement: Theorem 7.9.4. There is a unique continuous ρ^{χ,I,αβ,Q} : G_F → GSp_4(T^{χ,I,αβ,Q}) which is a deformation of ρ̄ of type 𝓢^{I,αβ}_{χ,Q} such that the induced R_{𝓢} → T is a homomorphism of Λ_I-algebras; this is the local–global compatibility the patching needs, including the ordinarity at v|p in the shape dictated by the doubling results. Corollary 7.9.6: for a cuspidal π of parallel weight 2 with central character |·|^2 which is ordinary, and p > 2, there is a continuous semisimple ρ_{π,p} : G_F → GL_4(Q̄_p) with the expected local–global compatibility at every finite place, extending Theorem 2.7.1 to the weight 2 case.

items.name: Lemma 7.9.7 and Proposition 7.9.8: Nakayama for perfect complexes and descent from level Q
items.statement: Lemma 7.9.7. A morphism of bounded complexes of m_Λ-adically complete separated flat Λ-modules which is a quasi-isomorphism after ⊗^L Λ/m is a quasi-isomorphism. Proposition 7.9.8: the natural map M^{χ,I,αβ,Q} → M^{χ,I,αβ} induces an isomorphism (M^{χ,I,αβ,Q})_{Δ_Q} → M^{χ,I,αβ}.

items.name: Proposition 7.11.2: the patched modules are maximal Cohen–Macaulay
items.statement: Proposition 7.11.2. M^{1,I,αβ}_∞ is a maximal Cohen–Macaulay module over (R^{1,I,αβ}_∞)', and M^{χ,I,αβ}_∞ is a maximal Cohen–Macaulay module over (R^{χ,I,αβ}_∞)'.

items.name: Lemmas 7.12.2 and 7.12.3: the cycle comparison for Ihara avoidance
items.statement: Lemma 7.12.2. For a finite O-flat R̃^1-module M^1 and a finite O-flat R̃^χ-module M^χ with M^1/λ ≅ M^χ/λ as modules over the common special fibre, the associated cycles agree. Lemma 7.12.3: under the further hypothesis that M^1 is supported on the relevant components, the cycle of M^χ is Σ_η d'_η·[η] with multiplicities d'_η independent of the modules and of the auxiliary ring (Remark 7.12.6), and these multiplicities receive a local representation-theoretic interpretation in Proposition 7.13.5. Remark 7.12.7 records that the idea of comparing patched modules over R^{1}_∞ and R^{χ}_∞ goes back to Taylor's Ihara avoidance.
