items.name: Hypothesis 7.13.1 and Definition 7.13.4: the hypotheses on ρ and the Iwahori and optimal levels
items.statement: Hypothesis 7.13.1 lists the standing hypotheses on the characteristic zero representation ρ : G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p): F is totally real with p ≥ 3 split completely; ν∘ρ = ε^{−1}; ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is pure at each finite v; ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary at each v|p; ρ̄ is vast and tidy; and ρ̄ is ordinarily modular in the sense recalled there. Remark 7.13.2: Hypothesis 7.13.1 implies Hypothesis 7.8.1 for ρ̄. Definition 7.13.4 fixes the tame levels K^{p,Iw} and K^{p,Iw_1}, Iwahori at the places of R, Iw_1 at the auxiliary place v_0, and hyperspecial elsewhere.

items.name: Proposition 7.13.5: the multiplicities d_{η_v} as sizes of L-packets
items.statement: Proposition 7.13.5. For a generic point η_v of Spec R_v^1 with v ∈ R, the set of y ∈ (Spec R_v^{1,η_v})(Ē) whose L-packet L(ρ_y) contains a generic representation is nonempty, and the number d_{η_v} = Σ_{π ∈ L(ρ_y)} dim π^{Iw(v)} is independent of y. This gives the local representation-theoretic interpretation of the multiplicities appearing in Lemma 7.12.3.

items.name: Theorem 7.13.6: the dimension of the space of p-adic forms at Iwahori level
items.statement: Theorem 7.13.6. Assume Hypothesis 7.13.1 for ρ = ρ_x. For any I with #I ≤ 1 and any choice of αβ, dim_E S^{I,αβ}_{κ_2,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}[p̃_x^{I,αβ}] = 8d_ρ, where d_ρ = ∏_{v∈R}d_{η_v} and the factor 8 = |W| arises because one works at Iwahori level at the auxiliary place v_0 without imposing conditions on the Hecke operators there (Remark 7.13.7). Lemma 7.13.8: for R one of the patched rings and M a maximal Cohen–Macaulay R-module, M_{p_x} is free at a smooth closed point x of Spec R[1/p]. Proposition 7.13.9 is the doubling injection (U_{w,1} − αβ'_w) : S^{I∪{w},αβ}[p̃_x] → S^{I,αβ}[p̃_x], and Proposition 7.13.11 computes the corresponding dimensions in regular weight. Remark 7.13.12 notes that the generic point multiplicity d'_ρ equals d_ρ and that a geometric Breuil–Mézard interpretation should be possible.

items.name: Theorem 8.2.1 and Corollary 8.2.2: gluing, and the automorphy of ρ
items.statement: Theorem 8.2.1. Assume ρ satisfies Hypothesis 7.13.1. Then for any I ⊆ S_p and any choice of αβ, dim_E S^{I,αβ}_{κ_2,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}[p̃_x^{I,αβ}] = dim_{C_p} S^{I,αβ,†}_{κ_2,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}[p̃_x^{I,αβ}] = 8d_ρ; that is, the classical and overconvergent spaces have the same dimension for every I, not only for #I ≤ 1. Corollary 8.2.2: consequently ρ is modular — there is an ordinary cuspidal automorphic representation π' of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 with ρ_{π',p} ≅ ρ and WD(ρ|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π'_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}) at every finite place v.

items.name: Lemmas 8.2.3 and 8.2.5: analytic continuation and descent of the glued forms
items.statement: Lemma 8.2.3. The elements of the eigenspace V_{αβ_1,αβ_2} extend to the larger adic space 𝓧^{mult,‡,d^H_1 ≥ 1−ε, d^H_2 ≥ 1−ε, d^L_1>1, d^L_2>1}_{Iw(v_1,v_2)} for some ε > 0, and similarly for the sums V_{αβ_1+αβ'_1,αβ_2} and V_{αβ_1,αβ_2+αβ'_2} on the corresponding spaces. Lemma 8.2.5: after shrinking ε, any element of V_{α_1,α_2+β_2} descends to 𝓨^{mult,‡,d^H_1 ≥ 1−ε, d^H_2 ≥ 1−ε}_{Iw(v_1)}. These are the analytic continuation and étale descent steps which, combined with the linear relations coming from doubling, produce a Klingen ordinary form on the whole rank ≥ 1 locus.

items.name: Lemmas 8.2.7, 8.2.8, 8.2.10, 8.2.11 and Corollary 8.2.9: connected components and the superspecial locus
items.statement: Lemma 8.2.7. A finite étale map of adic spaces of finite type over a field sends connected components onto connected components. Lemma 8.2.8: every connected component of Y^{I,=_{v_2}1} contains a point of Y^{I,=_{\{v_1,v_2\}}1}, and every connected component of Y^{I,=_{v_2}2} contains a point of Y^{I,=_{v_1}1,=_{v_2}2}; Corollary 8.2.9 deduces that every connected component of the two relevant adic spaces contains a point non-ordinary at v_1. Lemma 8.2.10: each irreducible component of Y^{=_{J^c}2,=_J1}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p,1} contains a point of the supersingular locus Y^{=_{S_p}0} in its closure, using that the Ekedahl–Oort stratification extends to the minimal compactification with affine open strata. Lemma 8.2.11 is the corresponding statement at Iwahori level, through the Kottwitz–Rapoport stratification; Remark 8.2.12 explains why a more direct proof is not available.

items.name: Lemma 8.3.1: the similitude character of an irreducible symplectic representation
items.statement: Lemma 8.3.1. Let K be a number field and ρ : G_K → GL_4(Q̄_p) irreducible preserving a generalized symplectic form with similitude character ν. Then either ν is uniquely determined by ρ, or, if ρ also admits the similitude character νψ with ψ ≠ 1, then ψ has finite order and ρ is reducible over a quadratic subfield of the field cut out by ψ.

items.name: Lemma 8.3.2: solvable descent for Hilbert–Siegel modular forms
items.statement: Lemma 8.3.2. Suppose p > 2 splits completely in the totally real field F, let F'/F be a solvable extension of totally real fields, and let ρ : G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) satisfy ν∘ρ = ε^{−1}, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary for all v|p, ρ̄ vast and tidy, and ρ|_{G_{F'}} irreducible and modular. Then ρ is modular. This is the solvable descent that makes Ihara avoidance usable.

items.name: Theorem 8.4.1: the main modularity lifting theorem
items.statement: Theorem 8.4.1. Suppose p ≥ 3 splits completely in the totally real field F and ρ : G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) satisfies: ν∘ρ = ε^{−1}; ρ̄ is vast and tidy; ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary for all v|p; ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is pure for all finite v; and ρ̄ is ordinarily modular, that is there is a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2, ordinary at all v|p, with ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄ and ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} pure at all finite v. Then ρ is modular. This is the theorem from which all the potential modularity results are deduced.

items.name: Definition 8.5.1 and Theorem 8.5.2: the version with relaxed central character
items.statement: Definition 8.5.1. A representation ρ : G_{Q_p} → GSp_4(Q̄_p) is twisted p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary if it is an unramified twist of one that is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary, and similarly for admissible representations of GSp_4(Q_p). Theorem 8.5.2 is Theorem 8.4.1 with ν∘ρ = χε^{−1} for a totally even finite order character χ unramified at all places above p, and the corresponding twisted hypotheses; this is the form used for the applications where the similitude character is not exactly inverse cyclotomic.

items.name: Definition 9.1.1: automorphic compatible systems over a general number field
items.statement: Definition 9.1.1. Let K be a number field and 𝓡 a strictly compatible system of representations of G_K. Then 𝓡 is automorphic if there is an automorphic representation Π of GL_n(A_K) which is an isobaric direct sum ⊞_{i=1}^rΠ_i of C-algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations, with prescribed infinitesimal characters, and such that for each finite place v and each λ one has WD(r_λ|_{G_{K_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec(Π_v ⊗ |·|^{(1−n)/2}). Remarks 9.1.2, 9.1.3 and 9.1.4 explain that the definition is partly redundant, that Π is already determined by the condition at almost all v, that no archimedean condition is imposed, and what is and is not known about upgrading the condition from almost all v to all v.

items.name: Definitions 9.1.6 and 9.1.8: automorphic and modular abelian varieties and GSp_4-representations
items.statement: Definition 9.1.6. An abelian variety A/K is automorphic if 𝓡_A is automorphic, and potentially automorphic if 𝓡_A|_{G_L} is automorphic for some finite extension L/K. Definition 9.1.8. For F totally real, ρ : G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) is modular if there is a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 with WD(ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}) at every finite v, and in particular ρ ≅ ρ_{π,p}; an abelian surface is modular if the associated ρ_{A,p} is. Remarks 9.1.7 and 9.1.9 explain the agreement of Gamma factors and conductors, and the relation between being automorphic and being modular, which depends on where π sits in Arthur's classification: modularity is only proved when the corresponding representation of GSp_4 is of general type.

items.name: Lemma 9.1.10: irreducibility and regularity for rank two compatible systems
items.statement: Lemma 9.1.10. For a rank two weakly compatible system 𝓡: (1) 𝓡 is irreducible if and only if every r_λ is irreducible, if and only if some r_λ is; (2) if 𝓡 is irreducible and regular then the analogous equivalences hold for the properties used in the potential modularity argument.

items.name: Propositions 9.1.11 and 9.1.12: Moret-Bailly and restriction of scalars
items.statement: Proposition 9.1.11. Let F_1/F be a finite extension of totally real fields and p, q > 2 distinct primes splitting completely in F_1. Given r̄ : G_{F_1} → GL_2(F̄_q) with determinant ε̄^{−1} which is locally of the displayed ordinary shape at each v|q, there is a finite Galois extension of totally real fields F'/F and an elliptic curve realising the prescribed mod p and mod q data, by an application of the theorem of Moret-Bailly to an auxiliary moduli space. Proposition 9.1.12 is the group-theoretic input: for a finite group G, a number field E, a finite set S of places, an extension E'/E and a linearly disjoint F_avoid/E, together with prescribed local Galois extensions H'_v/E'_v, there is a G-extension of E' with the prescribed local behaviour, obtained from Calegari's lifting argument by restriction of scalars.

items.name: §9.2: the classification of abelian surfaces by endomorphism type and challenging surfaces
items.statement: Following the standard classification of abelian surfaces over a field by their endomorphism algebras into types A, B[C_1], B[C_2], C, D, E, F, Proposition 9.2.1 shows that an abelian surface A/F which is not of type A or B[C_2] is potentially automorphic, since in the remaining cases A becomes of CM type or of GL_2-type over a finite extension and the compatible system is potentially abelian or reduces to lower rank. A challenging abelian surface is one of the remaining types, for which the new argument is needed.

items.name: Lemma 9.2.2: big image for abelian surfaces
items.statement: Lemma 9.2.2. If A/F is a challenging abelian surface then for a density one set of primes l the representation ρ̄_{A,l} is vast and tidy. If End_C A = Z this follows from Serre's theorem that ρ̄_{A,l}(G_F) = GSp_4(F_l) for all sufficiently large l together with Lemma 7.5.15; if A is of type B[C_2] one writes ρ_{A,l} as an induction and applies Lemma 7.5.22.

items.name: Definition 9.2.3 and Lemmas 9.2.5 and 9.2.6: good primes for an abelian surface
items.statement: Definition 9.2.3. A rational prime p ≥ 3 is a good prime for an abelian surface A/F over a totally real field if A admits a polarization of degree prime to p, p splits completely in F, ρ̄_{A,p} is vast and tidy, and ρ_{A,p}|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary at each v|p. Remark 9.2.4: these are exactly the primes at which the modularity lifting theorem applies. Lemma 9.2.5: for a challenging A the set of good primes has relative density one in the set of primes splitting completely in F. Lemma 9.2.6: there are distinct primes p, q both good for A such that ρ̄_{A,q}(Frob_v) has distinct eigenvalues for all v|p.

items.name: Lemma 9.2.7: the p–q trick and the global realization of a GL_2-representation
items.statement: Lemma 9.2.7. Let A/F be an abelian surface over a totally real field and p, q primes as in Lemma 9.2.6. Fix a totally real quadratic F_1/F in which p and q split completely, linearly disjoint from the fields cut out by A[p] and A[q]. Then there is a finite Galois extension of totally real fields F'/F and a representation r̄_q : G_{F_1F'} → GL_2(F̄_q) with inverse cyclotomic determinant whose induction to G_{F'} is ρ̄_{A,q}|_{G_{F'}} and which is modular, coming from an elliptic curve produced by Moret-Bailly. This is the version of Wiles's 3–5 trick used here.

items.name: Theorem 9.2.8: potential modularity of challenging abelian surfaces
items.statement: Theorem 9.2.8. Let A/F be a challenging abelian surface over a totally real field. Then A is potentially modular: there is a finite Galois extension of totally real fields F'/F and a prime p splitting completely in F' such that ρ_{A,p}|_{G_{F'}} is modular and irreducible.

items.name: Theorem 9.3.1 and Corollary 9.3.3: potential automorphy and meromorphic continuation
items.statement: Theorem 9.3.1. For F totally real and A/F an abelian surface, 𝓡_A is potentially automorphic and Conjecture 2.8.6 holds for A for each 0 ≤ i ≤ 4. The proof treats i = 1 and 2 and uses Brauer's theorem together with base change and the known functorialities in small rank; Remark 9.3.2 explains that the use of the results on GL_4 can be avoided by working with GSp_4 directly. Corollary 9.3.3: for a genus two curve C/F the completed Hasse–Weil L-function Λ(C,s) has a meromorphic continuation to C with Λ(C,s) = εN^{−s}Λ(C,3−s), ε ∈ R and N ∈ Q_{>0}.
items.locator: Theorem 9.3.1, Remark 9.3.2 and Corollary 9.3.3 (§9.3), Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Kim; Krishnamurthy)

items.name: Theorem 9.3.4: potential modularity of elliptic curves over quadratic extensions
items.statement: Theorem 9.3.4. Let K/F be a quadratic extension of a totally real field F and let E/K be a genus one curve or an elliptic curve. Then E is potentially modular: there is a Galois extension of totally real fields F'/F and a weight 0 cuspidal automorphic representation 𝛑 of GL_2(A_{KF'}) with trivial central character such that ρ_{E,l}|_{G_{KF'}} ≅ ρ_{𝛑,l} for every prime l. The proof applies Theorem 9.3.1 to the Weil restriction of scalars of E from K to F.
items.locator: Theorem 9.3.4, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501

items.name: Proposition 9.4.1 and Definition 9.4.2: Kummer and K3 surfaces, and F-abelian varieties
items.statement: Proposition 9.4.1. For an abelian surface A over a totally real field F and X = Km(A) the Kummer surface, Conjecture 1.1.1 holds for X: the odd cohomology vanishes and the even cohomology is generated by that of A together with the sixteen exceptional divisors, all of which are Tate classes. Definition 9.4.2: an F-abelian variety is an abelian variety A over a Galois extension E/F all of whose Gal(E/F)-conjugates are isogenous to A over E; when the conjugates are isogenous to quadratic twists of A, the Galois representation on Λ^2H^1 descends and the results apply. §9.4 also discusses the expected consequences for K3 surfaces over totally real fields with geometric Picard number at least 17.

items.name: Proposition 10.1.1: the modularity criterion for an ordinary abelian surface
items.statement: Proposition 10.1.1. Let F be a totally real field in which p > 2 splits completely and A/F an abelian surface with good ordinary reduction at all v|p whose unit root crystalline eigenvalues are distinct modulo p at each v|p. Assume A admits a polarization of degree prime to p, that ρ̄_{A,p} : G_F → GSp_4(F_p) is vast and tidy, and that ρ̄_{A,p} is ordinarily modular. Then A is modular, corresponding to a Hilbert–Siegel eigenform of parallel weight two. Remark 10.1.2 notes that if A has no polarization of degree prime to p then ρ̄_{A,p} is reducible, so the polarization hypothesis may be replaced by the irreducibility of ρ̄_{A,p}.
items.locator: Proposition 10.1.1 with Remark 10.1.2 (§10.1), Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501

items.name: Proposition 10.1.3 and Theorem 10.1.4: residually dihedral and induced cases
items.statement: Proposition 10.1.3. Let F be totally real with p > 2 split completely and ρ̄_p : G_F → GSp_4(F_p) absolutely irreducible with similitude ε^{−1}, vast, tidy and p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary. Suppose either (i) p = 3 and ρ̄_3 is induced from a two-dimensional representation with inverse cyclotomic determinant over a totally real quadratic E/F in which 3 is unramified, or (ii) p = 5 and the analogous GL_2(F_5) statement, or (iii) ρ̄_p is induced from a character of a quartic CM field in which p splits completely. Then ρ̄_p is ordinarily modular, so the modularity hypothesis may be dropped. Theorem 10.1.4 is the corresponding statement at p = 5 for an elliptic curve E/K over a quadratic extension K/F with good or semistable ordinary reduction above 5 and prescribed mod 5 image.

items.name: Theorem 10.2.1: every mod 3 GSp_4-representation is the 3-torsion of infinitely many abelian surfaces
items.statement: Theorem 10.2.1. Fix ρ̄ : G_F → GSp_4(F_3) with similitude character ε^{−1}. Then the twist B(ρ̄) of the Burkhardt quartic is unirational over F, and there exist infinitely many principally polarized abelian surfaces A/F up to twist with End_C(A) = Z and ı_3 : A[3] ≅ V(ρ̄)^∨; moreover these A may be taken to be Jacobians of curves with a rational Weierstrass point.

items.name: Definition 10.2.2, Proposition 10.2.3 and Lemma 10.2.4: the Burkhardt quartic and its degree six cover
items.statement: B = 𝓐_2(3) is the moduli space of principally polarized abelian surfaces with full level three structure, a compactification of which is the Burkhardt quartic; Definition 10.2.2 introduces the cover B(2) = 𝓐_2(6) → B with Galois group S_6 ≅ PSp_4(F_2), identified generically with the Galois group of the Weierstrass points. Proposition 10.2.3: the intermediate variety P is rational over Q, and there is a birational map P → P^3 over Q equivariant for the action of G, given by the odd theta map Th^-. Lemma 10.2.4: for ρ̄ : G_F → GSp_4(F_3) with similitude ε^{−1} the twist P(ρ̄) is rational, because the corresponding class in H^1(F,PGL_4) comes from H^1(F,GL_4), using that Sp_4(F_3) is the Darstellungsgruppe of PSp_4(F_3); Remark 10.2.5 records that the analogous facts for PSL_2(F_5) give a cleaner proof of the corresponding lemma of Shepherd-Barron and Taylor.

items.name: Theorem 10.2.6: infinitely many modular abelian surfaces over a totally real field where 3 splits
items.statement: Theorem 10.2.6. Let F be a totally real field in which 3 splits completely. Then there exist infinitely many abelian surfaces A/F up to twist with End_C(A) = Z which are modular and which do not come from any proper subfield of F, in the sense that for each p no twist of ρ_{A,p} extends to the absolute Galois group of a proper subfield.

items.name: Lemma 10.3.1 and Conjecture 10.4.3: the paramodular conjecture and its modification
items.statement: Lemma 10.3.1. Any abelian variety A/Q satisfying the hypotheses of Proposition 10.1.1 satisfies the paramodular conjecture: there is a holomorphic cuspidal Siegel newform of weight (2,2) and paramodular level equal to the conductor of A, which is a non-lift, has rational Hecke eigenvalues and is unique up to scalars. Conjecture 10.4.3 is the modified paramodular conjecture of Brumer–Kramer: for each N, the set 𝓐_N of isogeny classes of abelian surfaces A/Q with End_Q A = Z and conductor N, together with the set 𝓑_N of isogeny classes of fake abelian surfaces (QM abelian fourfolds) B/Q of conductor N^2 with End_Q B an order in a nonsplit quaternion algebra, is in bijection with the set 𝓟_N of suitable paramodular newforms of level N. The paper explains why the original formulation requires this modification.

items.name: Lemma 10.3.2: motives attached to automorphic representations, conditionally
items.statement: Lemma 10.3.2. Let F be a totally real field. Assume the Fontaine–Mazur Conjecture, the Standard Conjectures, the Hodge Conjecture, and that the Galois representations attached to any cuspidal automorphic representation Π of GL_4(A_F) whose infinity type at each v|∞ corresponds to the L-parameter φ_{2;1,0} form an irreducible weakly compatible system. Then the associated motive exists with the expected properties, which is what forces the modification of the paramodular conjecture recorded in Conjecture 10.4.3.

items.name: Expected Lemma 10.4.4 and Lemma 10.4.6: a fake abelian surface and an explicit genus two curve
items.statement: Expected Lemma 10.4.4. There exists a totally real field F, an indefinite quaternion algebra D and an abelian fourfold A/F with End_F(A) ⊗ Q = End_C(A) ⊗ Q = D; the proof is a sketch starting from the quaternion algebra over Q ramified exactly at 2 and 3. Lemma 10.4.6 exhibits an explicit genus two curve y^2 = Σ_{i=0}^6 a_ix^i over Q(√−6), with the a_i given by a table in terms of η = 1 − √−6, whose Jacobian realises the required behaviour; these are the examples and counterexamples that motivate the modified paramodular conjecture.

items.name: §1.4.2: why the method does not extend to curves of genus at least three
items.statement: Symplectic motives of rank 2g over Q are conjecturally attached to automorphic representations of the split orthogonal group SO_{2g+1}, replaced by GL_2 and GSp_4 for g = 1, 2 by the exceptional isomorphisms. The automorphic representations contributing to the Betti cohomology of locally symmetric spaces have regular infinitesimal character, so can only serve for g = 1; those contributing to the coherent cohomology of the orthogonal Shimura varieties are representations of the inner form SO(2g−1,2) whose infinity components are discrete series or non-degenerate limits of discrete series, which happens only for g ≤ 2. Equivalently, no Hodge–Tate weight of an automorphic vector bundle can occur with multiplicity greater than 2, while H^1 of a genus g curve has weights 0 and 1 each with multiplicity g. Picard curves y^3 = x^4 + ax^2 + bx + c are singled out as a genus three family to which the method should apply, through a form of U(2,1).

items.name: Abelian schemes, their duals, polarizations, torsion and the Weil pairing
items.statement: The moduli problem of §3.3 is built from abelian schemes A → S with an O_F-action, a prime-to-p quasi-polarization λ : A → A^t with prescribed kernel on A[v^∞], and level structures given by trivializations of the adelic Tate module compatible with the Weil pairing ⟨,⟩_λ. Isogenies, quotients by finite locally free subgroups, the dual abelian scheme and the Weil pairing between A[n] and A^∨[n] are used throughout, as is the fact that [n] is finite locally free of rank n^{2g}, étale exactly when n is invertible.
items.locator: §3.3, the moduli problem, and used throughout §§3–5, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: A1 constructs abelian schemes with rigidity, A2 the dual abelian scheme through Raynaud's theorem, the Poincaré bundle, biduality and polarizations with the exact hypotheses, and A3 the fppf quotient by a finite locally free subgroup, isogenies and their duals, and the Weil pairing with the alternating pairing induced by a polarization. That is exactly the abelian-scheme input this paper's moduli problem needs; the roadmap's summary says in as many words that it is the library required by Siegel, PEL and Hilbert modular varieties.

items.name: Serre–Tate and Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory and the de Rham realization
items.statement: The Serre–Tate theorem, identifying the deformations of an abelian scheme in characteristic p with those of its p-divisible group, is used repeatedly to compute the local structure of the Hecke correspondences at p, in the proofs that the normalized trace maps p^{−3}Tr_{u_1}, p^{−2}Tr_{r_1} and p^{−1}Tr_{s_2} exist and in the identification of U_{w,2} with the square of the partial Frobenius. The relative H^1_dR with its Hodge filtration and Gauss–Manin connection supplies the Kodaira–Spencer map of §5.5.
items.locator: Used in §§4.5, 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: A4 constructs relative H^1_dR with its Hodge exact sequence, Gauss–Manin connection and base change, and names Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory as an input from FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.6. Serre–Tate theory is the same deformation-theoretic package in the p-divisible group form.

items.name: Automorphic vector bundles and their canonical and subcanonical extensions
items.statement: The sheaves ω^κ on the open Shimura variety and their extensions ω^κ and ω^κ(−D) to a toroidal compactification, together with the pushforward to the minimal compactification used in every vanishing argument, are the automorphic vector bundles attached to algebraic representations of the Siegel Levi.
items.locator: §§3.7, 3.8, 3.10 and throughout §§4–6, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: B2 defines the bundle attached to a representation of the parabolic or Levi with its canonical-model descent, B3 the canonical extension on a toroidal compactification, the subcanonical extension 𝓥^{can}(−D) and the pushforward to the minimal compactification as a coherent sheaf. C4 plans degenerations of polarized abelian schemes and C5 the integral PEL toroidal and minimal compactifications with their universal semi-abelian extensions. What is not planned there, and is recorded as missing below, is the case of parahoric level at p, which C5 explicitly excludes by keeping the good-prime assumptions on the PEL datum.

items.name: Canonical subgroups and the degree function
items.statement: The adic spaces 𝓧_{K(p^n)}(ε) and the neighbourhoods 𝓧(J) of §6 are defined by bounds on the degrees of the canonical subgroups H_v ⊂ 𝓖_v[p^n] and on the degrees of the Iwahori-level subgroups L_v, and the whole dynamical analysis of the Hecke correspondences in §6.5 is an analysis of how U_{w,1} and U_{w,2} move these degrees. The existence, uniqueness, base change and isogeny compatibility of canonical subgroups on the Hasse neighbourhoods, and the behaviour of the Hasse radius under division by the canonical subgroup, are the inputs.
items.locator: §§6.1 and 6.5, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: T3 proves existence, uniqueness, base change and isogeny compatibility of canonical subgroups on the Hasse neighbourhoods with quantitative bounds, and the effect of division by the canonical subgroup on the Hasse radius; T4 owns the canonical and anticanonical geometry and the period estimates. The degree function of Fargues is the measure used in both.

items.name: The Hodge–Tate map, the modified integral lattice and the Hodge–Tate period
items.statement: The sheaves Ω^κ of §4.3 are defined through the Hodge–Tate map HT : H_∞ → ω_{𝓖}/p^n, whose determinant factors through ⊗_{v|p}Λ^2(O_{F_v}/p^n)^4 (Remark 6.2.2), and the modified integral lattice ω^{mod}_𝓖 and the canonical filtration Fil^{can} of §6.1 are built from it; the vanishing theorem of §6.2 is proved by pushing forward along the Hodge–Tate period map to an affine formal model of the minimal compactification.
items.locator: §§4.3, 6.1 and 6.2, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: T2 proves the Hodge–Tate exact sequence and its relative form, constructs the Hodge–Tate parabolic reduction and Levi torsor and the universal flag-valued map on a tower where the Tate module is trivialized, and for PEL data proves the filtration respects endomorphisms and the polarization. T5 owns the Igusa trivializations and the modified integral lattice, which is exactly ω^{mod}.

items.name: Adic spaces, formal models, generic fibres and coherent sheaves with traces
items.statement: All of §6 takes place on the adic generic fibres of the formal completions of the integral models, with the Hasse domains 𝓧(ε) as rational subdomains, admissible formal schemes and their admissible sheaves, Čech complexes of Banach modules, and the trace maps attached to finite flat morphisms of adic spaces.
items.locator: §6 throughout, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: R0 owns morphisms and admissible affinoid products, R2 formal schemes, their generic fibres and the Hasse domains by name, and R3 coherent sheaves and finite traces. These are the exact adic-geometric prerequisites of §6.

items.name: Fredholm theory, compact operators and slope decompositions on Banach modules
items.statement: Lemma 6.3.14 shows U^I is compact on the complex of overconvergent cuspidal forms and factors through the restriction maps; Theorem 6.3.16 deduces from Coleman's spectral theory that the Euler characteristic of the ordinary part is locally constant in the weight; and the finite slope subspaces of §6.5 are the slope decompositions attached to a compact operator on a Banach module over an affinoid algebra.
items.locator: §§6.3 and 6.5, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Coleman, p-adic Banach spaces and families of modular forms, §A5)
items.note: L4 plans continuity and compactness of the semigroup operators, nuclear and Fredholm determinants in the precise compact-operator setting, slope decompositions and their compatibility with specialization on slope-adapted affinoids; L2 plans the compact U_p action on affinoid modules and the classicality and control theorem in the small-slope range for GL_2. The operator theory is the same; what is missing here is the GSp_4 geometry it is applied to.

items.name: Moret-Bailly's rational points theorem
items.statement: The existence of rational points on a smooth geometrically irreducible variety over a number field, after a finite extension with prescribed local behaviour and prescribed real places, is the theorem which converts the twisted moduli spaces of §§9.1 and 10.2 into the required elliptic curves and abelian surfaces.
items.locator: Used in §§9.1, 9.2 and 10.2, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Moret-Bailly, Groupes de Picard et problèmes de Skolem II)
items.note: R23.1 is the Moret-Bailly milestone: the rational-point existence theorem for smooth geometrically irreducible varieties with prescribed nonempty local open sets and a finite extension satisfying the required disjointness and real-place conditions, including its geometric and approximation prerequisites rather than as an axiom.

items.name: Chebotarev and the general mechanism for choosing Taylor–Wiles auxiliary primes
items.statement: The construction of Taylor–Wiles data in Lemma 7.6.1 and Corollary 7.6.3 combines the Chebotarev density theorem, a residual-image lemma and the dual Selmer calculation to choose primes with prescribed Frobenius eigenvalues and q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N, reducing the dual Selmer group to zero with a uniform bound on the number of primes.
items.locator: Used in §7.6, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: R04.5 plans exactly this mechanism — Chebotarev, residual-image lemmas and dual Selmer calculations, the dual-Selmer dimension reduction and the uniform bound — and warns that adequacy, cyclotomic absolute irreducibility and enormous image are different hypotheses to be verified in the consumer. The GSp_4-specific verification, through vastness, is recorded as missing below.

items.name: The patching construction and the amplitude, depth and support inequalities
items.statement: Proposition 7.10.1 is the abstract patching criterion for defect l_0 ∈ {0,1}: from a system of rings R_N, finite quotients S_N of O[Δ_N] and modules or complexes M_N with uniformly bounded presentations one constructs a patched module M_∞ over S_∞ = Λ⟦x_1,…,x_q⟧ and the patched deformation ring R_∞, with the augmentation isomorphism recovering the original module and with depth at least dim S_∞ − l_0. Together with the balanced-module criterion of Definition 2.10.1 and Lemma 2.10.2 — that M is balanced, d_S(M) ≥ 0, if and only if it admits a presentation S^d → S^d → M → 0 — this is the Calegari–Geraghty modification of the Taylor–Wiles method.
items.locator: Definition 2.10.1, Lemma 2.10.2 and Proposition 7.10.1, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Calegari–Geraghty, Modularity lifting beyond the Taylor–Wiles method, Invent. math. 211 (2018), 297–433)
items.note: R03.5 plans the inverse-limit patching of finite-level rings, modules and transition data with the depth comparison; P8 plans patching of complexes with cohomology in several degrees, naming the ultrapatching construction, the uniform bounds and the augmentation isomorphism; P9 plans the inequalities relating codimension of support, projective dimension and Tor-amplitude and the balanced-dimension conclusions used in Calegari–Geraghty, together with the component-support transport used for Ihara avoidance. Proposition 7.10.1 and the balanced modules of §2.10 are exactly that material.

items.name: Global deformation functors, representability, local conditions and global presentations
items.statement: The deformation problems of §7.1, their representability, the framed variants and the torsor relating them, and the presentation of Proposition 7.2.1 of the global deformation ring over the local ones with the Galois-cohomological count of generators and relations, are the standard global deformation theory, here carried out for GSp_4-valued representations with a fixed similitude character.
items.locator: §§7.1 and 7.2, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: R04.1 and R04.2 plan deformation functors, representability and universal representations, R04.3 local conditions and global presentations, and G7 the polarized dimension-n problems with a fixed similitude or polarization character. The GSp_4 case with ν∘ρ = ψ is an instance; the local deformation problems specific to GSp_4 are recorded separately as missing.

items.name: Galois cohomology with restricted ramification, Poitou–Tate duality and Selmer groups
items.statement: The presentation of Proposition 7.2.1 and the Taylor–Wiles argument use the finiteness of H^i(F_S/F,−), Poitou–Tate duality, the Greenberg–Wiles formula for the dual Selmer group, and the local conditions defining the Selmer and dual Selmer groups attached to a global deformation problem.
items.locator: §§7.2, 7.5 and 7.6, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: R02.3 plans global finiteness and cohomology with restricted ramification, R02.4 Poitou–Tate duality, R02.5 Selmer groups with their local conditions, and R02.6 the cohomological requirements of patching.

items.name: Local deformation rings away from p and potentially semistable deformation spaces
items.statement: The unrestricted local lifting rings R_v^□ at v ∤ p, their generic fibres and smooth points, and the potentially semistable and fixed-inertial-type deformation spaces used for the Ihara avoidance rings R_v^χ are the general local deformation theory in the GSp_4 setting.
items.locator: §7.4, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: R08.1 plans the unrestricted local rings, R08.2 the places away from p and R08.3 potentially semistable deformation spaces with their components. What this paper adds — the explicit component analysis for GSp_4 through nilpotent orbits — is recorded as missing and routed there as a source.

items.name: Cyclic and solvable base change and descent for GL_2
items.statement: Solvable base change and descent for GL_2, with the exact criterion for failure of cuspidality and the local prescribed splitting consequences, is used in §9 to move the elliptic curve produced by Moret-Bailly between fields and, through Lemma 8.3.2, to descend Hilbert–Siegel modularity along a solvable extension.
items.locator: Used in §§8.3, 9.2 and 9.3, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: R17.4 plans cyclic base change and descent for GL_2 with local compatibility and the failure-of-cuspidality criterion, iterated to solvable extensions, and the local prescribed splitting consequences used by potential modularity. The GSp_4 analogue, Lemma 8.3.2, is recorded as missing.

items.name: The local Langlands correspondence for GL_2
items.statement: The correspondence rec between irreducible admissible representations of GL_2(K) and Weil–Deligne representations, with its compatibility with twisting, central characters and unramified representations, is used to state the local–global compatibility in Theorem 2.7.3, in the definition of automorphic compatible systems, and throughout the comparison of GSp_4 with GL_4.
items.locator: §§2.3, 2.7 and 9.1, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: R16.2 plans local smooth representation theory and R16.3 the local Langlands correspondence for GL_2. The correspondence for GSp_4, which is what the paper mainly uses, is recorded as missing.

items.name: Compatible systems of Galois representations and the operations on them
items.statement: The notion of a weakly and of a strictly compatible system, its purity, the independence of the Frobenius polynomials and the conductor, Brauer induction on compatible systems and the passage from potential automorphy over an extension to statements over the base field are the general machinery used in §§2.8 and 9.
items.locator: §§2.8, 9.1 and 9.3, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: R19.3 plans purity and compatible systems with the distinction between weak, almost strict and strict compatibility preserved; R24.5 and its operations sublayer plan the construction of a system over the original field from potential modularity by solvable base change, descent and character induction, and warn that a virtual linear combination from Brauer induction is not itself a representation — exactly the point at which Theorem 9.3.1 has to be careful.

items.name: Abelian varieties over a field
items.statement: An abelian variety over a field K is a proper smooth geometrically connected group scheme over K; the abelian surfaces A/F and the Jacobians of genus two curves which are the subject of the paper are abelian varieties of dimension 2 over a number field, and the compatible system 𝓡_A is built from H^1(A_{F̄},Q̄_l).
items.locator: §§1.1, 2.8, 9 and 10, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Tau Ceti has abelian varieties over a field as a structure, with the smoothness, geometric connectedness, commutativity and dimension API, and about two hundred further declarations around them. What it does not have, and what the moduli problem of §3.3 needs, is abelian schemes over a general base with their duals and polarizations; that is recorded separately as a planned item.

items.name: The symplectic group scheme Sp_{2n} with its root subgroups
items.statement: Sp_4 is the derived group of GSp_4 and is the group whose F_p-points appear throughout §7 in the enormousness and tidiness arguments, in the identification of the Darstellungsgruppe of PSp_4(F_3) in Lemma 10.2.4, and in the description of the residual images.
items.locator: §§2.1, 7.5 and 10.2, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Tau Ceti constructs Sp_{2m} as an affine group scheme over a commutative ring through its coordinate Hopf algebra, identifies its points with the symplectic matrices, and proves the Chevalley commutator relations for its root subgroups. It has no similitude group: a search of the pinned libraries for 'similitude' returns nothing, so GSp_4 itself is recorded as missing.
